Passed on September 26, 2022 by the General Education Committee in its 1st Provisional Meeting
of the 1st Semester of the 2022 Academic Year
Promulgated on December 27, 2022 by the official letter Cheng Jiao Zhi No. 1110041080
Passed on April 17, 2025
at the 1st General Education Committee Meeting of the 2nd Semester, Academic Year 2024-2025
Passed on April 17, 2025 by the General Education Committee in its 1st Meeting of the 2nd Semester
of the 2024 Academic Year.
Article 1 These directives are established in accordance with Article 13 of the
National Chengchi University Regulations for Awarding Outstanding
Teachers.
Article 2 The candidates for selection shall be faculty members as defined in the
University’s Regulations for Awarding Outstanding Teachers. The length
of teaching service shall be calculated up to the end of July of the academic
year preceding the selection.
Article 3 The awards for outstanding teachers are categorized into two types based on
the nature of teaching: professional courses and general education courses
(including physical education courses).
The award quota for teachers of professional courses in colleges is three-
quarters of the total awards, with the remaining quota allocated to general
education courses (including physical education courses).
Each award recipient will receive a commemorative gift and a grant of
NTD 60,000 from the University.
Article 4 The Center for General Education Teaching Excellence Selection
Committee (hereinafter referred to as “the Selection Committee”) consists
of nine members, comprising conveners of seven domain committees and
the Director of the Physical Education Office. The Director of the Center
for General education serves as the convener and manages the selection
matters.
If a committee member is nominated as a candidate for outstanding teacher,

this member shall not serve on the Selection Committee. The vacancy will
be filled by another appointment by the Director of the Center for General
Education.
Article 5 The award for outstanding general education teachers is given once every
academic year. The selection process is as follows:
1) Data Collection Phase:
a) The Office of Academic Affairs provides a list of courses ranked in the top
40% based on the statistical results of the teaching evaluation surveys from
the previous academic year (both semesters).
b) The Personnel Office, in conjunction with the Computing Center, conducts a
survey for outstanding teachers and provides a list of teachers ranked in the
top 50% and those who have passed the performance evaluation for the
current year.
c) When submitting the lists, the Office of Academic Affairs and the Personnel
Office shall also provide the detailed results of the respective surveys.
2) Nomination Phase by the Center’s Selection Committee:
a) Members of Selection Committee shall recommend candidates based on the
information outlined above and supporting evidence related to the
following specific criteria. Where necessary for deliberation, the
Committee members may request the University to provide additional
relevant information to facilitate the selection process.
1. Candidates who clearly articulate and effectively implement their
teaching philosophy and achieve outstanding teaching outcomes.
2. Candidates who design innovative teaching materials or instructional
websites, develop creative teaching methods, and publish these as
textbooks or reference materials with excellent results, and serve as
valuable resources for educators in related fields.
3. Candidates who successfully stimulate students’ interest in learning and
actively promote reading and academic engagement, and demonstrate
significant impact.
4. Candidates who provide regular academic advising and mentoring to
students, and effectively encourage their academic growth.
5. Candidates whose excellence in teaching is affirmed through peer
evaluations; if necessary, the Committee may establish a teaching
observation team for further assessment.

6. Candidates who have made substantial progress in enhancing their
professional expertise with demonstrable results.
7. The distribution of student performance assessments.
8. Effective use of digital teaching materials, instructional websites, and
multimedia teaching tools with notable effectiveness.
9. Other relevant teaching-related documentation.
b) Upon completing a comprehensive review based on the detailed investigation
results and supporting documents related to the aforementioned specific
criteria, the Selection Committee shall recommend a ranked list of candidates
not exceeding twice the number of available positions. The recommendations,
together with the recommendation forms, detailed investigation results, and
supporting documents, shall be submitted to the University Selection
Committee for deliberation.
Article 6 Faculty members who have not passed the University’s faculty performance
evaluation and have their evaluation results filed by the University Faculty
Evaluation Committee are not eligible for selection as Outstanding Teachers.
Article 7 The Outstanding General Education Teacher Survey is conducted among
undergraduate students who are enrolled during the period when the survey
system is open. The administration and scoring of the survey shall be carried
out in accordance with the University's relevant operational regulations.
Article 8 Teachers who have received the Outstanding Teaching Award three times in
total shall be designated as Distinguished Teachers and will receive a
monthly grant of NT$15,000.
The grant is awarded for a period of three years. During the three academic
years (inclusive) starting from the award year, the recipient shall not be
nominated again as an Outstanding Teacher. If the recipient is also awarded
a Distinguished Professor or Chair Professor grant, they may receive only
one of the grants.
Article 9 The accumulation of Outstanding Teaching Awards for the purpose of
Distinguished Teacher designation, as stipulated in the preceding article,
shall commence from the 2005 academic year and shall not be applied
retroactively.
Article 10 Meetings of the Selection Committee shall be convened only when more
than two-thirds of its members are present in person.

Article 11 These guidelines shall take effect upon approval by the General Education
Committee. The same procedure shall apply to any subsequent amendments.

Article 1 National Chengchi University Regulations for General Education Courses
(hereinafter referred to as the "Regulations") is established to regulate the
general education course offerings and to achieve the goal of holistic
education.
Article 2 The Center for General Education (hereinafter referred as the "Center") is
responsible for the university’s general education courses.
Article 3 National Chengchi University (hereinafter referred to as "NCCU") faculty
members and researchers shall follow the Regulations and relevant
regulations of NCCU when offering general education courses.
Article 4 General education courses at NCCU comprise of General Language

Education Courses, Common General Education Courses, and College
General Education Courses.
Article 5 The general education course structure and credit requirements are listed as
follows:
I. General language Education Courses contain Chinese Language Courses
(3 to 6 credits), and Foreign Language Courses (6 credits); Common
General Education Courses contain courses in Humanities (3 to 7
credits), Social Science (3 to 7 credits), Natural Science (3 to 7 credits),
and Informatics and Computing (2 to 3 credits); College General
Education Courses (0 to 3 credits). Students need to complete 28 credits
to satisfy the graduation requirements. Excess credits are not counted as
graduation credits.
II. Core General Education Courses, structured under the Common General
Education Courses, aim to cultivate vision, self-learning, independent
thinking, and civic awareness in students.
III. The core general education courses are offered in the domains of
Humanities, Social Sciences, and Natural Sciences. Students are
required to take at least one such course from two of the three above
domains respectively.
IV. The recognition, waver, and transfer of general education course credits
are handled in accordance with the University's General Education
Course Credit Recognition and Crediting Regulations.
V. General Language Education Courses shall be handled in accordance
with the university’s Regulations for Undergraduate English Courses,
Regulations for Enrollment in Foreign Language Courses, and
Implementation Guidelines for General Education Chinese Language
Instruction.
Students admitted before the 2017 academic year shall take at least 4 to 6
credits of foreign language general education courses.
Students admitted before the 2019 academic year shall follow the original
general education curriculum and complete 28 to 32 credits to satisfy the
graduation requirements. Excess credits are not counted as graduation
credits. The maximum credit granted for Common General Education
Courses of Humanities, Social Science and Natural Science respectively is
9 credits. The new general education courses of Informatics and Computing
are regarded as Common General Education Courses in Natural Science.
Starting from the 2024 academic year, international students enrolled in
fully English-taught degree programs or in departments that offer a
sufficient number of English-taught courses to fulfill graduation
requirements shall take general education courses in accordance with the
NCCU Guidelines for General Education Courses for International
Students Enrolled in English-Taught Programs.

Article 6 Offering of General Education Courses shall be aligned with the course
guidelines established by respective domain committees. The general
education courses at NCCU are offered in either one of the following ways:
I. By invitation: By following the NCCU philosophy and the objectives of
general education and with the approval of the President, the Vice
President for Academic Affairs, the Director of the Center, and the
convener of each domain group, the Director of the Center invites
NCCU instructors or request relevant colleges or departments to recruit
off-campus scholars and experts to offer courses.
II. Application for Course Offering: Only full-time and part-time faculty
members and full-time researchers of the university may apply. Self-
directed learning courses shall be administered in accordance with the
Guidelines for College General Education Courses for Self-Directed
Learning.
Article 7 Offering of general education courses shall comply with the following
principles.
I. In principle, a general education course is designed as a two-credit
course in each semester. Courses involving group discussions and
similar activities may be designed as three-credit courses.
II. The minimum number of students enrolled in a course is fifty. In
principle, the maximum enrollment for Core General Education Courses
shall be limited to 140 students.
III. No prerequisite courses are allowed.
IV. Exclusions shall be set for students enrolled in related departments. In
general education courses, students from departments or colleges
closely related to the course content shall be excluded as a principle. For
Core General Education Courses, students from the course-offering
department, as well as those pursuing double majors or minors in related
domains, shall be excluded from enrollment. If there are exceptional
cases, the reasons shall be clearly stated.
V. Except Core General Education Courses, a general education course
offers one class per semester in principle. Application for adding more
classes shall be submitted to the General Education Committee for
approval.
VI. Interdisciplinary courses may be designed and offered. Credit
recognition is limited to one single domain.
VII. Courses shall be offered according to the class hours and numbers of
subjects specified by the Center.
VIII. Core General Education Courses shall be offered as three-credit

courses. The instructor shall schedule one hour of discussion for every
two hours of lecture when the class is conducted in a group discussion
format. This discussion session shall be included in the official course
timetable and is included in the instructor’s total teaching hours,
amounting to three hours per course. Teaching assistants (TAs) of all
categories shall be assigned in accordance with the University’s TA
Implementation Guidelines and related regulations, following
application and approval procedures.
IX. General education courses shall be offered independently from
professional courses; cross-listing or alternating offerings between the
two is not permitted.
The rules in Items II, V, and VII of the preceding paragraph do not
apply to General Language Education Courses and interschool joint
general education courses.
Article 8 Those who apply to offer a general education course shall abide by the
following rules:
I. The instructor applying to offer a new general education course shall
submit the National Chengchi University Faculty and Researcher
Application Form for New General Education Course and related
documents to the Curriculum Committee of the corresponding
department and college or equivalent for approval before delivering to
the respective Domain Committee of the Center, the General Education
Committee, and the Academic Affairs Meeting for review.
II. Once a general education course has been approved through the relevant
committee reviews, any subsequent changes in the course content or
instructor are required to apply for approval in accordance with the
procedures for applying for a new course. Changes within three years of
approval shall be avoided.
III. Except for those offering Core General Education Courses, the course
offering application is required when the instructor has not offered the
same general education course for three or more years or more.
IV. A full-time faculty member may teach a maximum of four credits of
general education courses per semester. If core general education
courses are included, the maximum is six credits. This restriction does
not apply to full-time contract instructors assigned to specific teaching
duties.
Full-time researchers are required to meet the following additional rules
when applying to offer general education courses.
1. The applicant’s research unit shall submit the documents containing the
information on the applicant’s education and work experience to the

Faculty Evaluation Committee for review.
2. Applicants who pass the aforementioned reviews and receive approval
for their course offering proposals, as outlined in the previous
paragraph, will be submitted by the Personnel Office to the Ministry of
Education for issuance of teaching certificates. However, applicants
who are already qualified instructors may be exempted from this filing
procedure.
The review of teacher qualifications in the two preceding paragraphs
shall be conducted in accordance with the applicable personnel
regulations.
Article 9 The review procedure and criteria for general education courses are further
stipulated by the Center.
Article 10 Matters not specified in the Regulations shall be subject to the applicable
statutes and resolutions of the General Education Committee.
Article 11 The Regulations are implemented after approval by the General
Education Committee and the Academic Affairs Meeting. The same
applies to all subsequent amendments.

National Chengchi University
General Education Committee Establishment Regulations
December 21, 2020 Passed by the second Academic Affairs Meeting, fall semester, Academic Year 2020-21
Article 1 National Chengchi University (hereinafter referred to as “the University”) establishes the
General Education Committee (hereinafter referred to as “the Committee”) in accordance
with Article 8 of the University’s Organizational Regulations to plan and promote the
University’s general education and achieve the goal of holistic education.
Article 2 The functions of the Committee are as follows:
1. Deliberate on the general education system.
2. Revise the general education regulations.
3. Plan the development direction of general education courses.
4. Discuss and amend general education fields.
5. Review general education courses.
6. Address other matters related to general education.
Article 3 To respond to the development of general education courses, the Committee is divided into
the following domain groups, responsible for the planning, coordination, research, and
review of general education courses in their respective domains:
1. Chinese Language and Literature Domain Group.
2. Foreign Language and Literature Domain Group.
3. Humanities Domain Group.
4. Social Sciences Domain Group.
5. Natural Sciences Domain Group.
6. Information Domain Group.
7. College Education Domain Group.
The directives for each domain group shall be separately determined by the
Committee.
Article 4 The Committee consist of several members, with the following composition:
1. A convener, who shall be the Director of the Center for General Education.
2. The convener of each domain group.
3. One representative recommended by each college.
4. Two teacher representatives, recommended by the convener.
5. Two student representatives, recommended by the Student Association.
Article 5 The term of office for the Committee’s convener and the conveners of each domain group
shall be based on their respective terms of office; the term for college representatives and
1

teacher representatives is two years and may be re-elected once; the term for student
representatives is one year and may be re-elected once.
Article 6 The Committee shall convene at least once each semester, and the items resolved at the
meetings shall be submitted to the Academic Affairs Meeting for review.
Article 7 Instructors for general education courses may be invited by the Committee through
consultation with relevant colleges, departments, or institutes for appointment in
accordance with the University’s regulations on faculty appointment and promotion. This
Committee may recommend that relevant colleges, departments, or institutes appoint
part-time instructors for general education courses.
Article 8 These directives shall be promulgated and implemented after being passed by the
Academic Affairs Meeting, and the same applies for any amendment.

National Chengchi University Outstanding General Education
Professor Nominee Selection Regulations
Approved in the Academic Affairs Meeting of the 2nd
semester of 2006 on June 4, 2007
Article 1 The following regulations have been drafted in accordance with the
Ministry of Education National Outstanding General Education
Professor Selection and Incentive Guidelines in order to encourage
outstanding teachers to assist with general education, promote
achievements in teaching, and improve the quality of education.
Article 2 These regulations are applicable to full time professors who have taught
general education courses for at least six semesters.
Article 3 The Chengchi University Outstanding General Education Professor
Selection Committee has been established to select the University's
Outstanding General Education Professor.
The Center for General Education will nominate 7 committee members,
3 from outside of the University. The director of the Center for General
Education serves as an ex-officio member, and meeting chairs are
selected by committee members themselves. Two thirds of the
committee must be present at each meeting. Nominees for Outstanding
General Education Professor must receive fifty percent or more approval
from the committee.
Article 4 The selection of the University's outstanding general education
professor is governed by Ministry of Education National
Outstanding General Education Professor Selection and Incentive
Guidelines. The Outstanding general Education professor is to be
selected as follows:
1. Creation of selection committee
2. Eligible general education professors may submit their credentials
to the the Center for General Education
3. Each college selects a representative to participate in the selection
Article 5 Selection committee members will review course outlines, teacher
evaluations, grades, and other relevant materials to decide on
the nominees.
Article 6 The top three nominees for Outstanding General Education Professor
will be ranked, with number one being chosen as the University's

nominee. The selected professor is responsible for submitting any
further needed information. If the selected candidate declines, then the
following candidate will be chosen.
Article 7 Winners of the National Outstanding General Education Professor Award
are not eligible for re-selection for three years.
Article 8 Other matters will be handled according to Ministry of Education
regulations.
Article 9 These guidelines or their modifications are valid after approval by the
General Education Center Committee and the Educational Affairs
Committee.

NATIONAL CHENGCHI UNIVERSITY
Regulations for the Management of Distance Learning Classrooms
March 8, 2000 Passed by the 564th Administrative Meeting
2000 Promulgated via official letter Cheng Chiao Tzu No. 1301
Article 1 National Chengchi University (NCCU or “the University”) formulates the
NCCU Regulations for the Management of Distance Learning Classrooms
(“the Regulations”) to ensure proper management of the Distance Learning
Classrooms (“the Classrooms”).
Article 2 The Classrooms are exclusively for the use of distance learning and video
conferencing within the university.
Article 3 In addition to officially offered distance learning courses, other university
units may also use the Classrooms, subject to a fee, provided that normal
teaching activities are not affected.
Article 4 The operating hours for the use of the Classrooms during the semester are
as follows:
1. Monday to Friday: 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM.
2. Saturday (working day): 8:00 AM to 12:00 PM.
Any unit using the Classrooms outside of the abovementioned hours shall
be approved by the President.
Article 5 The use of the Classrooms, except for officially offered distance learning
courses, shall first be applied to the Instruction Resource Section of the
Office of Academic Affairs, and then payment shall be made at the Cashier
Section of the Office of General Affairs.
Article 6 The use of the Classrooms, except for officially offered distance learning
courses and those approved by the President, shall be subject to the
following fees (the fee standards are set separately):
1. Venue usage fee.
2. Network communication fee.

3. Personnel service fee.
Article 7 The user unit shall be held liable for any damage to the equipment in the
Classrooms caused by improper use or other human factors.
Article 8 The income and expenditure related to the use of the classroom shall be
managed under the University fund.
Article 9 The Regulations shall be passed by the Administrative Meeting, and then
promulgated and implemented by the President. Any amendments shall be
processed accordingly.

title: law61b.pdf
text:
NATIONAL CHENGCHI UNIVERSITY
Online Teaching Materials Production Guide
Digital Learning Promotion Committee
July 14, 2003
1. “Online teaching materials” refers to a method of distance learning, aiming to
allow instructors to create additional teaching materials beyond in-person content
for students to engage in self-directed learning via the internet.
2. The online teaching materials may include: detailed course outlines (such as
PowerPoint slides), recorded lectures (video or audio), relevant articles, case studies,
works by instructors and students, related website links, etc. These materials should be
sufficient for students to engage in self-learning or review the course content online.
The media formats for online materials may include text, images, video, audio, or
animation.
3. Full-time and part-time faculty members at the University may apply to the
Computer Center each semester for access to the distance learning platform,
regardless of whether they are applying for subsidies. They can use this platform
to create online teaching materials according to the needs of their courses. The
Computer Center provides consultation services to instructors.
4. Creating online teaching materials is a meaningful but time-consuming task. It is
advised that instructors consider the following factors when deciding whether to
provide online materials:
a. Will the online materials add value to the course or supplement any gaps in
the in-person teaching?
b. Is the content of the teaching materials complete enough for students to engage
in self-directed learning?
c. Will the online materials help maintain students’ interest in continuing to learn?
5. Faculty members who wish to apply for subsidy from the University shall submit
their application within the designated timeline and have it reviewed by the
Committee.
6. When reviewing subsidy applications, the Committee shall refer to the types and
quantities of materials proposed in the instructor’s plan and assess whether the
materials are complete, self-sufficient, and capable of providing teaching guidance. If
a course wishes to use an external platform not provided by the Computer Center, the
instructor shall provide an explanation and obtain approval from the Committee
before receiving the subsidy.
7. The online materials funded by the subsidy shall be comprehensive and capable of
providing teaching guidance:
a. “Complete” shall means that the material should be structured systematically
and clearly show the areas of knowledge and learning pathways. For example,
a complete online teaching material should cover all instructional units of the
course and clearly indicate the relationships between them.
b. “Providing clear teaching guidance” shall mean that the teaching material
producer should clearly indicate, through text or multimedia, the relationships

and usage of various resources, and where necessary, provide partial or full
explanations. For example, if the online materials provide an image, photo, or
video case study, the webpage should also introduce the background of the
work, explain its meaning, and possibly ask related questions to encourage
student reflection or discussion.
8. To ensure ease of downloading and reading, it is recommended that teaching material
producer converts document files (.doc), PowerPoint presentations (.ppt), and similar
file types into HTML format before uploading. If the format conversion affects the
presentation of the material, it is advised not to convert the file.
9. When the source files for the teaching materials are digital audio or video files,
the teaching material producer should appropriately compress them (e.g., convert
them into .wmv streaming file format) and apply to the Computer Center for use
of the streaming server (medias.cc.nccu.edu.tw). The teaching materials should
be provided via links.
10. If the online teaching materials include content from other sources (e.g., data from
a textbook CD or online resources), the producer should adhere to copyright law's
“fair use” guidelines and properly cite the source of the materials used.
11. If the online teaching materials funded by the subsidy include pre-made materials
by others, they should not exceed one-third of the course content. The teaching
material producer must clearly state in both the course webpage and the final report
which chapters of pre-made materials were used.

Directives for the Application and Review of Digital Learning
Programs
March 2, 2006 Promulgated by the MOE via official letter Tai Dien
Tzu No. 0950019586C

No. 0960057917C

Tzu No. 1040151683B
January 11, 2021 Amended by the MOE via official letter Tai Chiao Tzu

Article 1 The Ministry of Education (MOE) formulates the Directives for the
Application and Review of Digital Learning Courses (“the
Directives”) in accordance with the provision of Article 7 of the
Implementation Regulations Governing Provision of Distance
Education by Junior Colleges and Institutions of Higher Education,
in order to review and process the Digital Learning Programs (“the
Programs”) and provide learners with a channel for continuing
education through digital learning.
Article 2 The terms used in the Directives are defined as follows:
1. Overseas regions (“Overseas”): refers to regions outside of
Taiwan, Penghu, Kinmen and Matsu.
2. Digital Learning Programs (“the Programs”) referred to in the
Directives shall mean programs where students complete more
than half of the required credits for their degree through distance
learning. The classification of the Programs is as follows:
1) Digital learning in-service master’s programs: In

accordance with the Directives and subject to approval by
the MOE, the programs allow domestic and overseas
working professionals to take master’s degree courses
through digital learning channels, with degrees conferred in
accordance with the law.
2) Digital learning programs for overseas students: In
accordance with the Directives and subject to approval by
the MOE, the programs are jointly established with local
partner institutions abroad (excluding Mainland China) to
admit overseas students, offering two-year diploma
programs, bachelor's degree programs, master's degree
programs, and doctoral programs through digital learning
channels, with degrees conferred in accordance with the
law.
Article 3 Junior colleges and institutions of higher education offering the
Programs shall meet the following application requirements:
1. All junior colleges and institutions (“the institutions”), except
for the Open University, shall have necessary resources and
shall be limited to the institutions’ existing departments,
institutes, programs, or degree programs.
2. The Programs shall be approved by the relevant university-level
meetings.
3. For those collaborating with overseas educational institutions to
offer distance learning courses, it is limited to doing so with an
educational institution that is on the reference list of foreign

universities made public by the MOE, or one that has been
accredited by the local government authority for such
educational institutions or by the professional accreditation
agency for education in the country where it is located.
4. The institution shall not be a project school as specified in
Article 3 of the MOE Implementation Principles for the
Improvement and Discontinuation of Private Colleges and
Universities.
Institutions with any of the following conditions shall not be eligible
to apply for offering the Programs:
1. Institutions that fall under the conditions specified in Article 4,
Paragraph 1 of the Implementation Regulations Governing
Provision of Distance Learning by Junior Colleges and
Institutions of Higher Education, which prohibits the offering of
distance learning courses.
2. Project schools as specified in Article 3 of the MOE
Implementation Principles for the Improvement and
Discontinuation of Private Colleges and Universities.
3. Programs that fall under departments, institutes, or degree
programs that are subject to continuous monitoring or have not
been approved, as outlined in the MOE Notice for Ensuring
Students’ Rights in Junior Colleges and Institutions of Higher
Education.
Article 4 The application and review process for the Programs:
1. Each institution shall submit a program proposal, self-

assessment form and other relevant documents to the MOE for
review, in accordance with the application schedule announced
by the MOE each year. The application document formats,
submission methods and timelines shall be announced on the
MOE’s relevant website for the Programs.
2. The review process shall be carried out in stages, including
review of the application documents, review of the program
proposal and digital learning course content, and confirmation
by the MOE meetings.
Article 5 Faculty qualifications for the Programs and digital learning course
review requirements:
1. Faculty qualifications:
1) Faculty members shall meet the qualifications required for
university teachers and possess relevant experience in
digital teaching.
2) The departments responsible for the Programs shall comply
with the MOE faculty quality assessment standards.
3) Each institution shall operate in accordance with relevant
laws and regulations and ensure the research and teaching
quality of faculty members.
4) For digital learning programs for overseas students, local
instructors or industry experts may be hired based on
course needs. A specified percentage of the course shall be
taught by the institution’s full-time or part-time faculty, as
determined and communicated to each institution annually

by the MOE.
2. Digital learning course review:
1) The digital learning courses for the Programs shall be
submitted for review along with the program proposal.
2) The courses in the Program that passed the MOE digital
learning course review shall account for at least half of the
required graduation credits.
3. For approved Programs, any changes to course planning, partner
institutions, or course faculty shall be justified with supporting
documentation and submitted for approval by the MOE before
implementation:
1) A new review shall be conducted for approved programs if
changes to course planning exceed 30%.
2) Faculty changes for digital learning course review shall be
justified with explanations and accompanied by the
faculty’s relevant experience in distance learning course.
Such changes shall be submitted in advance through a
written application and may only proceed with approval
from the MOE.
3) For digital learning programs for overseas students,
changes to the overseas partner institutions or admission
plans shall require a revision of the program proposal,
which shall be approved by the MOE before admission can
proceed.
Article 6 Admission quotas and program types:

1. Digital learning in-service master’s programs:
1) For domestic working professionals, the quota shall be
included within the total admission quota. The applying
institution may adjust the allocation within this total,
subject to MOE review.
2) For overseas working professionals, the quota may be
processed as additional and may not be counted toward the
total admission quota.
3) Each Program (including tracks) shall have a maximum of
30 students.
2. Digital learning programs for overseas students:
1) The quota may be processed as additional and may not be
counted toward the total admission quota.
2) Day division and continuing education 2-year junior
college programs: Each Program shall have a maximum of
60 students.
3) Day division and continuing education bachelor’s
programs (including two-year and programs longer than
four years): Each Program shall have a maximum of 60
students.
4) Day division master’s programs: Each Program (including
tracks) shall have a maximum of 30 students.
5) Doctoral programs: Each Program (including tracks) shall
have a maximum of 5 students.
Article 7 Target applicants and eligibility requirements:

1. Digital learning in-service master’s programs:
1) Target applicants: The admission targets domestic and
overseas working professionals:
a. People of the Taiwan Area who hold a passport of the
Republic of China (ROC).
b. International students who have legitimate resident
status in Taiwan.
c. Hong Kong and Macao residents who have obtain
legitimate resident status in Taiwan for reasons other
than education.
d. Hong Kong and Macao residents residing overseas.
e. People of foreign nationality residing overseas.
f. People of the Mainland China area residing overseas.
2) Eligibility requirements: Applicants must hold a bachelor’s
degree or possess equivalent qualification and meet the
working experience requirements specified by each
institution.
2. Digital learning programs for overseas students:
1) Target applicants:
a. Hong Kong and Macao residents residing overseas.
b. People of foreign nationality.
c. People of the Mainland China area residing overseas.
2) Eligibility requirements:
a. 2-year bachelor’s programs: Graduate from junior
colleges or above or possess equivalent academic

ability.
b. 2-year junior college and 4-year or more bachelor’s
programs: Graduate from high schools or above or
possess equivalent academic ability.
c. Master’s programs: A bachelor’s degree or equivalent.
d. Doctoral programs: A master’s degree or equivalent.
3) Those who have academic credentials from overseas or
equivalent academic ability shall be handled in accordance
with the MOE’s Regulations Governing the Assessment
and Recognition of Foreign Academic Records by
Institutions of Higher Education, Standards for
Recognition of Equivalent Educational Levels for
University Admission, Standards for Recognition of
Equivalent Academic Ability for Junior College Admission,
and other relevant regulations.
4) Applicants for the Program who are found to have
submitted falsified, altered, borrowed, misused, or false
documents regarding their employment status, experience,
or years of service shall have their admission rescinded. If
already enrolled, their student status shall be revoked, and
they shall bear legal responsibility.
Article 8 Admission methods:
1. Each institution shall establish an admission committee to
oversee the admission process. All admission procedures shall
adhere to the principles of fairness, impartiality, and

transparency.
2. The admission of the Programs shall be handled in accordance
with Article 24 of the University Act and Article 19 of its
Enforcement Rules.
3. The admission regulations of each institution shall specify the
composition of the admission committee, the admission quota,
eligibility requirements, entrance exam methods, admission
selection process, admission dispute and appeal handling
procedures, rights and obligations of applicants, and other
matters to be followed.
Article 9 Matters related to recognition of academic records, recognition of
equivalent academic ability, duration of studies, student status,
required credits for graduation, and the granting of degrees shall be
handled in accordance with relevant laws and regulations and the
respective institution’s academic rules.
Article 10 Tuition and fees collection:
1. The collection of the tuition and fees for the Programs shall be
determined by each institution, taking into account teaching
costs, and shall be handled in accordance with the Regulations
Governing Tuition and Fees Collection at Junior Colleges and
Institutions of Higher Education. The tuition and fees may
include charges for the use of the digital learning platform. All
revenues and expenditures shall comply with relevant
accounting regulations, and the fee structure shall be specified
in the admission guidelines.

2. The fees for international students enrolling in the Program shall
be handled in accordance with Article 21 of the Regulations
Regarding International Students Undertaking Studies in
Taiwan.
Article 11 For digital learning in-service master program, students who are
Hong Kong and Macau residents residing overseas, people of foreign
nationality, or people of the Mainland China area residing overseas,
shall be subject to substantive review by the respective institution if
they intend to take certain courses within the territory of the ROC If
the evaluation is satisfactory, and if the students are not in violation
of public order or established custom, do not pose a threat to national
security, public interest, the health of the general public, or give rise
to concerns of any major occupational hazard occurring, relevant
documents and materials may be submitted to the MOE for reference
at least one month prior to the start of the course period.
The aforementioned documents and materials are as follows:
1. Official document from the applying institution.
2. Basic information of the aforementioned students, which shall
include student name, gender, birthday, nationality, passport
number, institution and department, residence address within
the ROC, and residence address either within their home
country (region) or outside of it.
3. A photocopy of the students’ passport.
4. A certificate from the attending institution confirming the
students’ enrollment and that course completion is required for

graduation.
The official document from the institution as mentioned in the first
item, in addition to being submitted to the MOE for reference, shall
be handled in accordance with the following conditions:
1. People of foreign nationality residing overseas may apply for a
visa through the ROC’s overseas missions. The decision to
approve or reject the application shall be determined at the
discretion of the respective mission.
2. Hong Kong and Macao residents residing overseas shall be
handled in accordance with Article 11 of the Regulations
Governing Permits for Hong Kong and Macau Residents
Entering and Residing in the Taiwan Area.
3. People of the Mainland China area residing overseas shall be
handled in accordance with Article 3 of the Regulations Governing
Permits for People of the Mainland China Area Entering the
Taiwan Area regarding short-term professional exchanges.
Students mentioned in the first item shall not alter their enrolled course
content or transfer to another institution while taking courses within the
ROC. During the course period, students shall strictly comply with the
laws and regulations of the ROC and shall not engage in activities or
employment unrelated to their course content. In the event of a violation,
and upon verification by the MOE, the matter shall be reported to the
National Immigration Agency, Mainland Affairs Council, and other
relevant authorities, and be notified to the Bureau of Consular Affairs at
the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and other relevant authorities.

Article 12 Hong Kong and Macao residents enrolling in the aforementioned
Programs do not fall under the category of those approved by the
central competent authorities for studying in Taiwan, as stipulated in
Article 16, Paragraph 1, Subparagraph 7 of the Regulations
Governing Permits for Hong Kong and Macau Residents Entering
and Residing in the Taiwan Area.
Article 13 The Programs which are established in alignment with national
diplomatic policies to admit international students may be exempt
from the restrictions specified in these Directives regarding
admission methods, prospective students, application methods for the
Programs, review process, and digital learning course review
requirements. Such Programs shall be implemented upon approval
from the MOE:
1. The applying institution shall have one year of experience in
offering the Programs, and the Programs being applied for shall
comply with the standards in the Program proposal review
criteria.
2. The quota may be processed as additional and may not be
counted toward the total admission quota.
3. Each Program (including tracks) shall have a maximum of 30
students.

National Chengchi University Regulations for the Implementation of
Micro-Credit Course
December 16, 2019 Passed by the 2nd Academic Affairs Meeting, fall
semester, Academic Year 2019-20
February 13, 2020 Promulgated via official letter Cheng Chiao Tzu No.
1090003494
Article 1 National Chengchi University (NCCU or “the University”) formulates
the NCCU Regulations for the Implementation of Micro-Credit Course
(“the Regulations”) to promote instructional innovation among teachers,
broaden students' international perspectives, and encourage students to
engage in interdisciplinary, diverse, and self-directed learning.
Article 2 The “micro-credit course’’ (“the courses”) referred to in the
Regulations includes various types of courses, such as digital courses,
social practice, interdisciplinary projects, industry sharing sessions, and
internship visits, offered by all teaching units of the University.
Instructors of the courses shall be full-time or part-time faculty of the
University, and the teaching hours for the courses shall not included in
the basic teaching hours. Furthermore, the instructors shall be
compensated on an hourly basis in accordance with the Ministry of
Education regulations, with related expenses supported by government
subsidies or the University's self-raised funds.
Article 3 The "micro-credit" referred to in the courses is based on a unit of 0.2
credits, with 3 hours of instruction equating to 0.2 credits.
Article 4 The courses should take into consideration students' learning needs and
the right to choose courses. Plans must be made with caution, and the
teaching syllabus should specify teaching objectives, course content,

schedule, teaching methods, and assessment criteria.
Courses opting for a "Pass/Fail" grading method must be approved by
the Academic Affairs Meeting.
Article 5 The establishment and review of the courses, upon the consent of the
authority responsible for course offering, shall be submitted along with
the teaching syllabus to the Micro-Credit Course Review Committee
(“the Committee”) of the University for review and approval before
instruction can proceed.
Article 6 The Committee shall consist of five to nine members, with the Vice
President for Academic Affairs serving as an ex officio member and the
convener. Other members shall be scholars and experts within or
outside the University recommended by the Vice President for
Academic Affairs, along with student representative. Committee
members shall serve a term of one year and be eligible for
reappointment upon expiration.
Article 7 For undergraduate students taking the courses, up to 4 credits can be
counted towards graduation credits. For master's and doctoral students,
up to 2 credits can be counted towards graduation credits. The credits
shall be counted according to the regulations of their respective
departments and faculties.
Article 8 Matters not addressed herein shall be handled in accordance with the
University's Academic Regulations and other applicable regulations.
Article 9 The Regulations shall be passed by the Academic Affairs Meeting and

then promulgated and implemented. Any amendments shall be
processed accordingly.

Implementation Regulations Governing Provision of Distance Learning
by Junior Colleges and Institutions of Higher Education
September 8, 2006 Promulgated by the MOE via official letter Tai San
Tzu No. 0950130239C
June 20, 2016 Amended by the MOE via official letter Tai Chiao Tzu
(2) Tzu No. 1050067651B
March 29, 2019 Amended and Promulgated via official letter Tai
Chiao Kao Tung Tzu No. 1080038536B
Article 1 These Regulations have been formulated in accordance with the
provisions of Article 30 of the University Act and Article 35 of the
Junior College Act.
Article 2 In these Regulations the term “distance learning” refers to teaching and
learning conducted by instructors and students using media such as
telecommunication networks, computer networks, and video channels.
In these Regulations the term “distance learning course” refers to single
subjects in which one half or more of the number of teaching hours are
undertaken in distance learning mode.
The number of teaching hours of the distance learning courses referred
to in the preceding paragraph includes the hours of lectures, interactive
student-instructor discussions, tests, and other learning activities.
Article 3 Junior colleges and institutions of higher education (hereinafter referred
to as “educational institutions”) offering distance learning shall
designate a unit that will be responsible for handling distance learning
matters and, if a course requires it, may arrange for a teaching assistant
to help with the teaching, or provide assistance to produce teaching
materials.
Article 4 Educational institutions providing distance learning shall do so using a
learning management system which is equipped to handle distance

learning implementation, students’ learning performance records, and
other learning support functions.
Article 5 If an educational institution offers distance learning courses, the unit
that will offer a course shall draft a course plan in accordance with the
educational institution’s regulations, and in accordance with the
provisions of the Enforcement Rules of the University Act and the Junior
College Act regarding curriculum planning and evaluation procedures,
the course plan shall be submitted to an educational institution-level
committee and may be offered if it is approved. Each approved course
plan shall be posted on the internet.
The course plan referred to in the preceding paragraph shall clearly state
the course objectives, the target students, a course outline, how students
will access the course, interaction and discussion between students and
instructors, performance evaluation methods, and matters to pay
attention when participating in classes.
Article 6 If a student completes a distance learning course with satisfactory
results and the calculation of the credits is in accord with the provisions
of the Enforcement Rules of the University Act and the Enforcement
Rules of the Junior College Act, the educational institution will award
credits for the course and include those credits in the total credits for
graduation.
The total number of credits awarded for completing distance learning
courses referred to in the preceding paragraph is not permitted to exceed
half of the credits required for graduation.
Article 7 Educational institutions which offer digital learning in-service Master’s

program shall apply for review and approval from the Ministry of
Education (“the MOE”) in accordance with relevant regulations. The
program shall be implemented only upon approval. The calculation of
total graduation credits for these programs is not subject to the
restrictions specified in the second paragraph of the preceding article.
The enrollment quota for each digital learning in-service Master’s
program is limited to 30 students per class. The MOE may specify the
validity period for program offerings and enrollment. Enrollment quotas
for these programs shall be included in the institution’s total enrollment
capacity as approved by the MOE; however, additional quotas may be
permitted upon the MOE’s approval.
Graduation certificates for digital learning in-service Master’s program
shall indicate that the mode of instruction was distance learning.
Article 8 If an educational institution plans to offer distance learning courses
cooperatively with an educational institution overseas, it is limited to
doing so with an educational institution overseas that is on the reference
list of foreign universities made public by the MOE, or one that has
been accredited by the local government authority for such educational
institutions or by the professional accreditation agency for education in
the country where it is located.
Article 9 Educational institutions shall carry out regular evaluations of the
distance learning courses they are offering and the results of offering the
courses. The regulations governing such evaluations shall be set by each
educational institution.
Educational institutions shall keep the evaluation reports produced in

accordance with the provisions of the preceding paragraph for at least
five years.
Article 10 The MOE may visit an educational institution to inspect or evaluate the
results of its distance learning. If the inspection results identify any
shortcomings or lack of compliance with regulations, the MOE shall
notify the educational institution that it must take corrective action
within a prescribed period. If the educational institution does not do so,
the MOE may, based on relevant regulations, reduce part or all of the
educational institution’s incentive awards or funding subsidies or
prohibit the educational institution offering its distance learning courses.
Article 11 Distance learning courses offered by open universities shall be handled
in accordance with the provisions of the Open University Establishment
Act, rather than these Regulations.
Article 12 These Regulations shall be implemented on the date of promulgation.

National Chengchi University MOOCs Course Development
Regulations
April 15, 2015 Passed by the Digital Learning Promotion Committee at

January 3, 2022 Passed by the 2nd Academic Affairs Meeting, fall

February 10, 2022 Promulgated via official letter Cheng Chiao Tzu No.
1110003205
Article 1 National Chengchi University (NCCU or “the University”) formulates
the NCCU MOOCs Course Development Regulations (“the
Regulations”) to encourage faculty members to create digital courses
and develop distinctive online teaching courses, which align with the
international education trends to enhance learning efficacy and promote
versatile applications.
Article 2 The MOOCs referred to in the regulations shall be Massive Open
Online Courses (MOOCs) or Small Private Online Courses (SPOCs).
Digital courses are designed with several small unit videos based on
weekly teaching progress, with each video lasting about ten minutes.
The total length of the course videos can be flexible, typically ranging

from six to eight hours. Besides videos, the course content should
include mechanisms such as digital platform interaction and assessment.
Article 3 Full-time and part-time faculty members of the University can apply to
offer courses on their own initiative or through the recommendation of
the colleges to which they belong. Relevant course plans should be
submitted to the Center for Teaching and Learning Development ("the
Center") according to the announced schedule each semester before
offering the course. After approval and announced by the Center, the
Center will provide assistance in course production.
Article 4 The instructor responsible for the course may employ one teaching
assistant before the recording of the course, and one after the course is
uploaded to the platform to assist in planning the course, producing
materials, recording videos, and managing the platform.
Article 5 The support, assistance, and rewards for instructors offered by the
Center are as follows:
1. The Center assists instructors in course planning, materials
production, video recording, and platform management, and
provides consultation for intellectual property regulations.
2. The subsidy for new course instructors and external lecturers is
calculated based on the completed video length, with each ten
minutes as a unit, each unit receiving a maximum subsidy of
NT$1,600, and the subsidy for each case is capped at eight hours.
During the course offering period, the incentive subsidy for

instructors is based on a principle of NT$10,000 per course.
3. During the course production period, the subsidy for course
assistants is calculated based on the completed video length, with
one hour as a unit, each unit receiving a maximum subsidy of
NT$2,000, and the subsidy for each case is capped at eight hours.
4. During the course offering period, the subsidy for each course
platform assistant is calculated based on the number of weeks of
classes, with one week as a unit, each unit receiving a maximum
subsidy of NT$1,500, and capped at four units per month.
5. The funding sources for subsidies related to the application for
MOOCs courses offered by the Center are government subsidies
or the University's self-raised funds.
6. The subsidy distribution method for co-offered courses is
negotiated by all participating instructors.
7. The Center may select high-quality MOOCs as the University’s
excellent digital courses for rewards.
Article 6 Instructors receiving support and awards from the Center must
comply with the following conditions:
1. Instructors must complete all lecture preparation,
proofreading, question setting, and assessment design
according to the timetable agreed with the Center. In
principle, no extensions can be requested for any reasons, and

the course content production must comply with the
regulations related to intellectual property rights.
2. The subsidized courses must be fully executed at least once.
3. During the course execution period, course content and
homework consultations should be provided on the digital
course platform, and teaching assistants should be arranged to
interact with students and manage discussion areas.
4. The subsidized instructors should participate in relevant course
and teaching development workshops organized by the Center
to share their experiences.
Article 7 The intellectual property rights of the completed courses belong to the
University, while the moral rights belong to the course instructors.
Article 8 MOOCs that have received subsidies from agencies outside the
University are not eligible to apply for the awards and subsidies listed in
the regulations.
Article 9 These regulations shall be passed by the Digital Learning Promotion
Committee and the Academic Affairs Meeting and then promulgated
and implemented. Any amendments shall be processed accordingly.

Article 1 National Chengchi University (NCCU or “the University”) formulates the
NCCU Directives for the Awards and Subsidies of Digital Learning (“the
Directives”) in accordance with Articles 5, 9, and 10 of the NCCU
Regulations for the Implementation of Digital Learning.
Article 2 Course Offering Procedures for Distance Learning Course
1. The instructor shall submit a course plan and syllabus in accordance with
the University’s prescribed format, and the mode of instruction shall be
stated clearly.
2. The aforementioned course shall be submitted to the department or
institute, and then to the college. Within the Office of Academic Affairs’
course offering procedure and timeline, the course documents shall be
submitted to the Center for Teaching and Learning Development

(CTLD) for review by the Digital Learning Promotion Committee (“the
Committee”). The review criteria shall be set separately.
3. The course may be offered after approved by the Committee and passed
by the Academic Affairs Meeting.
Article 3 Principles for Rewards and Subsidies
1. Additional Hourly Lecture Fee
For synchronous video broadcast general education courses, each credit
shall be counted as 1.5 hours. For courses that have already been
approved for additional hourly lecture fee, the calculation is as follows:
original lecture hours multiplied by 1.5, plus the approved additional
hours.
2. Course Assistant Subsidy
Distance learning courses with 30 or more enrolled students are eligible
to apply for one course assistant to support the operation of the courses.
The assistant shall be employed by the instructors themselves and shall
be a currently enrolled student at the University; the subsidy is NT$6,000
per month per person, with a maximum duration of four months per
semester. Courses with more than 70 enrolled students may receive an
additional 0.5 times the subsidy, and courses with more than 120
enrolled students may receive an additional full subsidy; a maximum of
two course assistants may be allocated per course. The assistant shall
choose only one type of funding, either from this subsidy or other
available compensation for assistants at the University.
3. Outstanding Digital Learning Course Award
To encourage faculty at the University to engage in digital learning, the
Committee may conduct a selection for outstanding digital learning

courses within the budget allocated each semester. Outstanding courses
may be awarded, funded by government subsidies or the University’s
self-raised funds. The amount for the award shall be determined based
on annual budget allocation.
Regulations regarding the award amount, selection method and criteria
shall be set separately by the Committee.
Article 4 Matters not addressed herein shall be processed in accordance with
University’s Regulations for the Implementation of Digital Learning, as well
as applicable regulations and relevant meeting decisions.
Article 5 The Directives shall be passed by the Academic Affairs Meeting, and
then promulgated and implemented by the President. Any amendments
shall be processed accordingly.

Article 1 National Chengchi University (NCCU or “the University”) formulates the
NCCU Regulations for the Implementation of Digital Learning (“the
Regulations”) in accordance with the Ministry of Education (MOE)’s
Implementation Regulations Regarding Distance Learning by Universities to
promote digital learning environment and provide students with divers
learning channels.
Article 2 “Digital learning” referred to in the regulations shall mean teaching and
learning activities between instructors and students conducted through digital
technologies.
Article 3 “Distance learning” referred to in the regulations shall mean teaching and
learning activities between instructors and students conducted over
telecommunications networks, computer networks, video-on-demand (VoD)

channels and other media.
“Distance learning courses” referred to in the regulations shall mean subjects
of which 50% or more of the instructional hours are conducted via distance
learning.
The aforementioned distance learning hours shall include lectures, teacher
student interactions and discussions, examinations, and other learning
activities.
Article 4 The University shall establish Digital Learning Promotion Committee (“the
Committee”). The Committee shall consist of members appointed by the
President, including the Vice President for Academic Affairs, the
Director of Computer Center, the Director of the Center for Teaching
and Learning Development, and other relevant teachers. Committee
members shall serve a term of two years and be eligible for
reappointment upon expiration, and the Vice President for Academic
Affairs shall serve as the convener. The Committee is responsible for
the planning, review, subsidy and assessment of distance learning
courses and other related matters.
Article 5 The instructor offering a distance learning course at the University shall
submit a syllabus and develop a course plan in accordance with the
University's regulations. The plan shall be reviewed by the Committee and,
after passed by the Academic Affairs Meeting, the course may be offered and
announced online.
Article 6 Distance learning courses shall be conducted via a learning management
system, which shall provide functions for course delivery, tracking student
learning progress, and other additional learning support.

Article 7 Depending on course requirements, distance learning course instructors may
assess students’ performance by administering mid-term and final exam or
with reports, assignments, and periodic tests. Mid-term and final exams shall
take place in a classroom.
Article 8 The course content on the distance learning course website, including
syllabus, teaching materials, records of teacher student interactions,
assessment records, attendance logs, and assignments, shall be submit to the
Committee after the end of the semester for the assessment of the courses and
their teaching effectiveness. The regulations for this assessment shall be
formulated separately by the Committee. The assessment report produced in
accordance with the preceding regulations shall be retained for at least five
years, and serve as a reference for grade inquires or site visits.
Article 9 The principles of the subsidies related to digital learning courses shall be
formulated separately by the Committee.
Article 10 Students who pass the distance learning courses shall be awarded credits,
which may count towards the total credits required for graduation. However,
the credits earned from distance learning courses shall not exceed half of the
total credits required for graduation.
Article 11 The digital learning in-service Master’s program shall be established in
accordance with the relevant regulations concerning the application, review,
and accreditation for such programs. The course shall be submitted to MOE
for review, and it may only be offered after obtaining MOE’s approval. The
calculation of graduation credits for the program shall not be subject to the
limitations outlined in the preceding Article. The degree certificate shall
specify that the mode of instruction for the program is through distance

learning.
Article 12 The course evaluation survey of digital learning courses shall be conducted by
the Office of Academic Affairs before the end of each semester. The teaching
outcomes of digital learning courses shall be evaluated by the Committee after
the courses end to assess teaching effectiveness. Courses evaluated as
outstanding may receive awards, with the award criteria set separately by the
Committee.
Article 13 For distance learning courses co-offered by the University and foreign
universities, the partner institutions shall either be listed in the MOE’s
Database for the Reference List of Foreign Universities, or be recognized by
educational authority of the local country or a professional academic
evaluation organization recognized by it.
Article 14 Matters not addressed herein shall be processed in accordance with MOE’s
Implementation Regulations Regarding Distance Learning by Universities,
the University’s Academic Regulations and applicable regulations.
Article 15 The Regulations shall be passed by the Academic Affairs Meeting, and
then promulgated and implemented by the President. Any amendments
shall be processed accordingly.

Article 1 National Chengchi University (NCCU or “the University”) Office of
Academic Affairs formulates the NCCU Teaching Assistant Funding
Subsidy Directives (“the Directives”) to assist faculty in enhancing

teaching quality and improve the teaching skills of teaching assistants.
Article 2 The Directives apply to teaching assistants currently enrolled at the
University, subsidized by the Office of Academic Affairs’ Center for
Teaching and Learning Development (CTLD) and the General
Education Center (GEC), whose application, review, and subsidy
follow the Directives.
Article 3 The review of funding support for teaching assistants is managed by the
Teaching Assistant Funding Review Committee (“the Committee”) of
the Academic Affairs Office. The Committee consists of the Vice
President for Academic Affairs, the Vice President for Student Affairs,
the Director of CTLD, and the Director of GEC, with the Vice
President for Academic Affairs as the convener. The review meetings
are held each semester, and subsidies are based on the number of
applied subjects and funding status.
Article 4 The application period, condition, and units are as follows:
1. Application Period: Applications should be submitted during the
announced period at the end of each semester.
2. Application Conditions and Units:
1) Discussion class, exercise class, and practical class teaching
assistants:
Courses with more than 35 enrolled undergraduate students
are eligible to apply. The course instructor should apply
according to the course planning. CTLD is responsible for
applications for integrated courses, college foundational

courses, departmental introductory courses, and specialized
courses; GEC is responsible for core general education
courses.
2) Course management teaching assistants:
For integrated courses, college foundational courses,
university-level foreign language courses, general education
language courses with more than 35 enrolled students,
regular general education courses with more than 60 and
undergraduate specialized courses with more than 70
students (the total number can be cumulative for the same
instructor and course across different sessions), and
departmental introductory courses with more than twenty,
the applications shall be complied by the course offering unit
and submitted to CTLD.
3) In-Service Program, Program, or Minor Courses:
Courses that require fees are not eligible for this type of
subsidy. As a principle, subsidies will not be provided
for expanded minor courses
4) Adapted physical education course teaching assistants:
The course offering unit should submit applications to
the CTLD.
Article 5 The review process is as follows:
1. For the application of discussion class, exercise class, practical

class, and course management teaching assistants processed by
CTLD:
1) For integrated courses, college foundational courses,
departmental introductory courses, and specialized courses,
applications are reviewed by the teaching assistant subsidy
application review meeting held by CTLD.
2) For course management teaching assistants, applications
shall undergo a preliminary vetting based on the following
criteria and then be submitted to the teaching assistant
subsidy application review meeting for review.
a. Course syllabus uploaded within the specified deadline.
b. The course's survey scores from the last two years
should be at least one standard deviation below the
average for all types of courses.
c. For courses without prior survey scores within the
last two years and with over 60 enrolled students.
3) Core general education course teaching assistants are
reviewed by the core general education course review
meeting held by GEC.
4) The subsidized course list approved by CTLD and GEC
shall be submitted to the Teaching Assistant Funding
Review Committee of the Office of Academic Affairs for
review.
Article 6 Principles for subsidizing teaching assistants:
1. Discussion class and exercise class teaching assistants:

1) For discussion class, one teaching assistant is subsidized for
every 35 enrolled students, and so forth; an additional
assistant is subsidized if the final enrollment number of
students exceeds 30.
2) For exercise classes, one teaching assistant is subsidized for
course enrollments between 35 and 85 students; if
enrollment exceeds 85 students, an additional teaching
assistant is subsidized for every additional fifty students.
3) The number of teaching assistants subsidized is based on the
number of students of the initial enrollment, and employment
should start from the first day of the term. Additional teaching
assistants may be recruited and employed based on funding
availability if enrollment numbers reach the above thresholds
after the add/drop period.
4) A maximum of four teaching assistants are subsidized per
course.
2. Practical class teaching assistants: Based on initial enrollment,
one teaching assistant is subsidized for every 35 students, with
employment starting from the first day of the term.
1) Course management teaching assistants:
For courses passed through the preliminary vetting and
meeting the subsidy standards, each course offering unit is
allocated a subsidy amount. Course offering units may set
their own standards within budget limits to determine the
subsidy for the courses.

2) If the course offering units intend to hire students with
disabilities as course management teaching assistants, which
may result in insufficient funding, they may apply for
additional subsidies.
3) Adapted physical education class teaching assistants: One
teaching assistant per class.
4) Each course may only accept subsidies from one funding
source.
Article 7 Salary and work-hour standards for teaching assistants are as follows:
1. Discussion class and exercise class teaching assistants:
1) Master’s and doctoral students: 10 hours per week per
course, 40 hours per month. Undergraduate students in their
fourth year or above, recommended by the course instructor,
may serve as teaching assistants, with 9 hours per week per
course, 36 hours per month.
2) Salary calculation principles: Monthly salaries are calculated
based on the hourly rate, with the following standards:
undergraduate students are paid in accordance with the basic
hourly wage approved by the central governing authority;
master’s students are limited to 1.2 times the rate for
undergraduate students; doctoral students are limited to 1.5
times.
3) The monthly salary of teaching assistants from each

academic system shall not be less than that of the previous
academic level. The semesterly salary of teaching assistants
is announced after approval by the Teaching Assistant
Funding Review Committee.
2. Practical and adapted physical education class teaching assistants:
A monthly salary of 6,000 TWD for each course, with an
increase of 3,000 TWD for enrollments exceeding 70 students
and an additional 6,000 TWD for enrollments exceeding 105
students.
3. Course management teaching assistants: The monthly salary shall
not be less than 6,000 TWD. This is not applicable to those who
also serve as discussion class, exercise class, or practical class
teaching assistants.
4. The total weekly work hours for an individual should not exceed
20 hours (up to 25 hours for doctoral students), with a maximum
of 4 months of salary disbursement per semester. The average
hourly wage should not be less than the basic wage announced by
the central governing authority.
Article 8 Responsibilities and obligations of discussion class, exercise class, and
practical class instructors and teaching assistants:
1. Discussion class and exercise class teaching assistants should
arrange a fixed time for each week to conduct the discussion or
exercise class (excluding the opening week, mid-term examination

week, and final examination week), with each class session lasting
50 minutes as the principle. Practical class teaching assistants
should assist the instructor in class or arrange a fixed time outside
of regular classes to guide students in practical work.
2. Those serving as teaching assistants for the first time must pass the
beginning-of-the-term instructional training course. Those who are
unable to attend must complete a make-up course on the
designated platform within one month of employment. Instructors
must submit a written report explaining the reasons if the teaching
assistant fails to complete the make-up course within the deadline.
3. Teaching assistants must submit a personal reflection report in
mid-term and collaborate with the instructor to compile a course
achievement final report. If plagiarism or other inappropriate
content is found in the personal reflection report, the instructor
will be notified and will be recommended not to employ the
assistant in subsequent semesters.
4. Each semester, teaching assistants must attend at least two
school-internal or -external teaching training courses and
teaching achievement sharing seminars organized or approved
by CTLD or GEC.
5. Teaching assistants shall cooperate with arrangements made by
CTLD or GEC for classroom observations.
6. Instructors receiving subsidies for the first time must attend an

orientation on the Teaching Assistant System.
Article 9 Evaluation and rewards for seminar and exercise class teaching
assistants:
1. Classroom observations should be conducted at least once each
semester; mid-term and end-of-term teaching assistant evaluations
should be arranged.
2. The end-of-term teaching evaluation for teaching assistants is
measured with a 5-point scale, with scores below 3 serving as a
reference for future employment decisions. Instructors must
submit a written report explaining the reasons for low scores.
3. After each semester, the effectiveness of subsidized courses is
evaluated based on the semester’s execution results, response rates
to the teaching assistant opinion survey, and the end-of-term
teaching evaluation results of teaching assistants. This evaluation
serves as a reference for future subsidies.
4. Excellent and Outstanding teaching assistants are selected
according to the University’s Regulations for the Election for
Excellent and Outstanding Teaching Assistants and are rewarded
accordingly, with the instructor also receiving a certificate.
Article 10 Matters not addressed herein shall be handled in accordance with
applicable regulations.
Article 11 The Directives shall be passed by the Teaching Assistant Funding

Review Committee and then promulgated and implemented. Any
amendments shall be processed accordingly.
