Article 1 National Chengchi University (NCCU or “the University”) formulates the
NCCU Regulations for the Selection of Outstanding and Excellent Teaching
Assistants to dedicated and outstanding teaching assistants, recognize their
teaching expertise and contributions, and enhance the teaching quality of
teaching assistants.
Article 2 The teaching assistants referred to in the Regulations shall be the discussion
class, exercise class, and practical class teaching assistants defined in the
NCCU Teaching Assistant System Implementation Regulations.
Article 3 The selection of Outstanding and Excellent Teaching Assistants shall be
conducted based on course categories, with the Center for Teaching and
Learning Development (CTLD) and General Education Center (GEC) each
establishing a Teaching Assistant Review Committee (“the Committee”) to

handle the selection process.
1. The selection of Outstanding and Excellent Teaching Assistants for
integrated courses, college foundational courses, departmental introductory
courses, and specialized courses shall be reviewed by the Committee
established by CTLD. The Committee shall be composed as follows:
1) The Vice President for Academic Affairs and the Director of CTLD
shall serve as ex officio members.
2) At least three internal or external faculty shall be appointed by the
Vice President for Academic Affairs as review committees.
3) At least two teaching assistants shall be recommended by the Director
of CTLD and appointed by the Vice President of Academic Affairs.
2. The selection of Outstanding and Excellent Teaching Assistants for core
general education courses shall be reviewed by the Committee established
by GEC. The Committee shall be composed as follows:
1) The Vice President for Academic Affairs and the Director of GEC
shall serve as ex officio members.
2) The convener of the respective general education fields meeting and at
least two internal or external faculty shall be appointed by the Vice
President for Academic Affairs as review committees.
3) At least two teaching assistants shall be recommended by the Director
of GEC and appointed by the Vice President of Academic Affairs.
3. The Vice President for Academic Affairs shall serve as the convener of the
above Committees, and the meeting shall be held at the end of each
semester.
4. Based on the principle of recusal of conflicts of interest, if an ex officio
member’s course is assigned with a teaching assistant for that semester, that

member shall not participate in the evaluation and discussion.
Article 4 The selection process for Outstanding and Excellent Teaching Assistants shall
be proceed as the following stages:
1. Stage 1 Review: Teaching assistants who meet the following criteria may be
selected as candidates and undergo written review:
1) Complies with the regulations outlined in Article 8 of the University’s
Teaching Assistant Funding Subsidy Directives.
2) The response rate to the teaching assistant evaluation survey is 40% or
higher, and the score exceeds the overall average score.
2. Stage 2 Final Selection: The Committee shall conduct a second review based
on the candidates shortlisted in the first stage. Based on the student
feedbacks, course instructors’ supplemental evaluation notes of the teaching
assistant's performance, and supporting materials submitted by each
candidate, the Committee shall assign scores to determine the final list of
Outstanding and Excellent Teaching Assistants.
Article 5 For integrated courses, college foundational courses, departmental introductory
courses, and specialized courses, the number of Outstanding Teaching
Assistants shall be limited to 3 per semester, while the number of Excellent
Teaching Assistant limited to 12. For core general education courses, the
number of Outstanding Teaching Assistants shall be limited to 1 person per
field each semester, and the total number of Excellent Teaching Assistants
shall be 12 in principle.
Article 6 The selected Outstanding and Excellent Teaching Assistants shall be shall be
publicly commended in the following semester.
1. Each Outstanding Teaching Assistant shall receive a certificate and a cash
prize of NT$6,000.

2. Each Excellent Teaching Assistant shall receive a certificate and a cash
prize of NT$1,000.
Article 7 Those who have been awarded as Outstanding Teaching Assistant three times
shall receive a certificate of “three times as the Outstanding Teaching
Assistant”. Those who have been awarded as Outstanding Teaching Assistant
five times shall receive a certificate of “five times as the Outstanding Teaching
Assistant” and no longer be eligible for nomination in future selections.
Article 8 The awarded teaching assistants shall share their teaching insights in relevant
events held by CTLD and GEC.
Article 9 The Regulations shall be passed by the Teaching Assistant Funding Review
Committee and then promulgated and implemented. Any amendments shall be
processed accordingly.

Article 1 National Chengchi University (NCCU or “the University”) formulates
the NCCU Teaching Assistant System Implementation Regulations
(“the Regulations”) to enhance students' professional and teaching
skills and to assist faculty in improving teaching quality.
Article 2 Teaching Assistant Definition
A Teaching Assistant refers to an individual who assists teachers in
teaching activities and is responsible for course discussions, exercises,

practical work, or supporting teaching-related activities.
Article 3 Types of Teaching Assistants
1. Discussion Course Teaching Assistant: Primarily responsible for
planning course group discussions according to the syllabus,
designing discussion topics and teaching materials, and leading
students in group discussions.
2. Exercise Course Teaching Assistant: Primarily responsible for the
planning of course exercise sessions according to the syllabus,
guiding students through exercises and clarifying questions
according to the teacher’s teaching progress.
3. Practical Course Teaching Assistant: Primarily responsible for the
planning of practical training sessions according to the course,
leading students in field surveys, computer software training, lab
experiments, equipment operation, practical safety maintenance,
technical coaching, and consulting, and supporting teachers in
innovative practical teaching methods.
4. Course Management Teaching Assistant: Primarily responsible
for preparing teaching materials, collecting information,
classroom management, student assignment assessment and
grading, academic advising, organizing teaching activities, and
assisting teachers in innovative teaching methods.
5. Academic Counseling Teaching Assistant: Primarily responsible for
assisting students with learning difficulties through one-on-one
academic counseling outside of class hours. When necessary, they

must coordinate with the Higher Education Sprout Project to record
and report case study learning statuses.
The tasks mentioned above may be adjusted in accordance with the
teaching needs of the faculty or the needs of the assisted students.
However, faculty or students may not request teaching assistants to
undertake matters unrelated to teaching, nor may they substitute for
teachers in lecturing or completing assignments on students’ behalf.
Article 4 Qualifications for Various Types of Teaching Assistants
1. Discussion and Exercise Course Teaching Assistants: Master's
students or above of the University.
2. Practical Course, Course Management, and Academic Counseling
Teaching Assistants: Undergraduate students in their third year or
above of the University.
Article 5 Rights and Responsibilities of Teaching Assistants and Teachers
1. In accordance with the announced standards for various types of
teaching assistants, teachers shall discuss with teaching assistants the
work items, salary, hours, and location. Upon agreement, a labor
contract shall be signed, and the work shall then be carried out in
accordance with the contract.
2. The term of employment each semester is principally four months,
with employing units having the discretion to adjust the number of
months employed according to their needs.
3. Relevant insurance and labor issues shall be handled in accordance
with the University’s Scholarship and Student Labor-type Assistant
Rights Protection Handling Regulations.

4. Teaching assistants must respect gender equity, adhere to professional
ethics, and strictly comply with the Gender Equity Education Act,
Gender Equality in Employment Act, Sexual Harassment Prevention
Act, and Regulations on the Prevention of Sexual Assault or Sexual
Harassment on Campus, among other applicable regulations.
5. Should a teaching assistant fail to perform duties in accordance with
the labor contract or violate teaching ethics or school regulations, the
teacher may submit a request to the funding unit to terminate the
contract.
6. During the employment period, matters concerning insurance,
intellectual property rights of research results, or related complaints shall
be handled in accordance with the University’s Scholarship and Student
Labor-type Assistant Rights Protection Handling Regulations.
Article 6 Matters not addressed herein shall be handled in accordance with
applicable regulations.
Article 7 The Regulations shall be passed by the Teaching Assistant Funding
Review Committee and the Academic Affairs Meeting and then
promulgated and implemented. Any amendments shall be processed
accordingly.

title: law119b.pdf

NATIONAL CHENGCHI UNIVERSITY
Office of Academic Affairs
Directives of the Implementation of Teaching Assistant Classroom
Observation
August 11, 2020 Passed by the Teaching Assistant Funding Review
Committee at its meeting of 2020
September 4, 2020 Promulgated via official letter Cheng Chiao Tzu No.
1090065776
Article 1 National Chengchi University (NCCU or “the University”) Office of
Academic Affairs, Center for Teaching and Learning Development
(CTLD) and General Education Center (GEC) formulates the NCCU
Office of Academic Affairs Directives of the Implementation of
Teaching Assistant Class Observation (“the Directives”) to effectively
manage and evaluate teaching assistants and enhance overall teaching
quality.
Article 2 Teaching assistant classroom observation refer to in the Directives
involves observing the teaching performance of all types of teaching
assistants subsidized by CTLD and GEC, as well as documenting
classroom observations and providing teaching feedback and
suggestions.
Article 3 Teaching assistant classroom observation shall be conducted through
the assistance of temporary personnel. The tasks include attending TA
classes, writing observation records and submitting the records to
CTLD or GEC.
The duty of temporary personnel may be adjusted based on the needs of
CTLD and GEC. The employment guidelines are as follows:
1. Qualification: Individuals who have been awarded or nominated
as Excellent or Outstanding Teaching Assistant.

2. Classroom observation duties:
1) Attend the class in-person.
2) Write observation records.
3) Provide feedback and suggestions to CTLD or GEC and
submit written materials.
3. Salary and working hours:
1) Temporary personnel for classroom observation may be
employed for up to 28 days per month, with compensation
based on the number of observation activities conducted. A
total of 3 to 6 observation activities is required, with 3 to 4
working hours per session, NT$300 per hour.
2) The total weekly working hours at the University shall not
exceed 20 hours for Master’s students and 25 hours for
doctoral students.
4. Notes:
1) Temporary personnel for classroom observation who also
serve as teaching assistants shall ensure that observation
schedules do not overlap with their teaching assistant duties.
Additionally, they shall avoid observing teaching assistants
assigned to the same instructor.
2) If it is discovered that teaching assistants are not conducting
exercise or discussion classes as required, or if there are
discrepancies between the reported schedules/locations and
actual conditions, the issue shall be promptly reported and
alternative observation times arranged.

3) If the observation records do not meet the required
standards, the temporary personnel may be asked to revise
and resubmit their work.
5. Rights and rewards and penalties:
1) If the temporary personnel for classroom observation who
also serve as teaching assistants perform well upon review,
they may be granted an exemption for attending one
teaching assistant activity for the semester.
2) Temporary personnel for classroom observation shall
comply with the regulations of CTLD and the University to
ensure the rights of the teaching assistants being observed.
Any involvement in plagiarism, falsification of observation
records, or other improper conduct may result in the
termination of their employment, depending on the severity
of the situation.
Article 4 The Directives are funded by government subsidies or the University's
self-raised funds.
Article 5 Matters not addressed herein shall be handled in accordance with the
other applicable regulations or announcement of the University.
Article 6 The Directives shall be passed by the Teaching Assistant Funding
Review Committee and then promulgated and implemented. Any
amendments shall be processed accordingly.

National Chengchi University Office of Academic Affairs Center for
Teaching and Learning Development Academic Counseling
Implementation Directives
March 11, 2020 Passed by the Seed of Hope Cultivation Project Review
Meeting for Self-Directed Learning Activity Subsidy
Application, spring semester, Academic Year 2019-20
April 20, 2020 Promulgated via official letter Cheng Chiao Tzu No.
1090010356

Project Review Meeting for Subsidy Application and
Academic Counseling Teaching Assistants
March 28, 2022 Promulgated via official letter Cheng Chiao Tzu No.
1110008877
July 7, 2023 Amended Articles 3,4 passed by the Seed of Hope
Cultivation Project Review Meeting for Subsidy
Application and Academic Counseling Teaching
Assistants
August 9, 2023 Promulgated via official letter Cheng Chiao Tzu No.
1120024668
Article 1 The Center for Teaching and Learning Development (“The Center”) of
the Office of Academic Affairs at National Chengchi University
(NCCU or “the University”) formulates the NCCU Academic
Counseling Implementation Directives (“the Directives”) to assist
students in improving their learning outcomes and to train outstanding
students to serve as academic counseling teaching assistants.
Article 2 The Center shall establish an Academic Counseling Review Committee
(“the Committee”), with the Vice President for Academic Affairs
serving as the convener, and three to five teachers invited to serve as
members to review tutoring subjects, academic counseling teaching
assistants, and related expenses.
Article 3 Academic Counseling
1. Counseling Target: Undergraduate students enrolled in the current
semester.

2. Counseling Subjects: Priority is given to courses that have not
received teaching assistants resource by the Center.
3. Counseling Time:
1) Counseling time is to be determined by both the tutoring
teaching assistant and the tutee.
2) Each tutoring session should last for one hour as a principle.
3) Academic counseling should commence upon approval and
before mid-term exams. If half of the total tutoring hours are
not completed within two weeks after the mid-term exams,
the counseling qualification will be canceled.
4. Counseling Location: The Center provides a learning space as a
principle.
5. Application for the Center’ learning spaces:
1) Applications are made through an online reservation.
2) Reservations open four weeks before the tutoring starts and
are available until the day before, with one time slot
available for reservation per group.
3) For cancellations, they must be made before the tutoring
session; failure to cancel twice will result in disqualification
for academic tutoring for the semester.
4) Notes on Counseling:
a. The tutees should prepare questions in advance and
focus on the subjects provided for tutoring.
b. During the tutoring period, the academic counseling
teaching assistant assists the tutee with tutoring but

shall not complete assignments on the tutee’s behalf.
c. Tutees are required to fill out a “Counseling Learning
Feedback Form” during the semester.
d. Students who have successfully applied for the “Seeds
of Hope Cultivation Program - Academic Counseling”
subsidy for the current semester at NCCU have priority
in arranging academic counseling tutoring
appointments.
Article 4 Academic Counseling Teaching Assistant
1. Eligibility: Third-year undergraduate students and above with
professional competence and recommended by a teacher.
2. Application Documents: Application form and transcript shall
be submitted during the application period to the Center.
3. Application Period: From the start of each semester until the
end of February or September.
4. Review Mechanism: The Committee decides the number of
hires based on the current semester's subject needs and budget
for the current semester, giving priority to applicants with
interdisciplinary and diverse skills.
5. Salary and Working Hours:
1) The monthly salary for undergraduate students must not
be less than NT$6,000; for Master's students, not less
than NT$7,000; and for Doctoral students, not less than
NT$8,000.
2) Those also serving as discussion class, exercise class,

practical class, or course management teaching assistants
are not subject to these limits, provided the average
hourly wage is not below the minimum wage announced
by the Ministry of Labor of the Executive Yuan.
3) The maximum working hours per month must not exceed
20 hours.
6. Responsibilities and Obligations:
1) Participate in two training workshops at the beginning and
end of the semester.
2) Assigned by the Center to conduct one-on-one academic
counseling tutoring at designated locations, assisting tutees
in their academic learning without completing tasks for
them. If there is no need for one-on-one tutoring, they agree
to perform other academic counseling-related duties as
arranged by the Center.
3) After each tutoring session, the teaching assistants should
complete an “Academic Counseling Record Form” to
document tutees’ learning status.
4) In case of an inability to conduct tutoring, leave must be
requested before 5 p.m. the day before, with make-up
sessions arranged later; for unforeseen circumstances
preventing prior leave request, the Center must be notified
immediately for a later make-up session.
5) If any problems arise during the academic counseling
process and cannot be resolved through mutual

communication between the teaching assistant and the tutee,
the Center should be notified immediately for intervention.
7. Rewards and Penalties:
1) Those with good performance, who submit an end-of-
semester tutoring experience report and adhere to
attendance and leave regulations, will be awarded a service
certificate by the Center at the end of the semester.
2) Teaching assistants must adhere to all regulations and
tutoring standards of the Center to protect the rights of the
tutees. Serious violations of professional requirements and
ethics may result in the termination of their teaching
assistant qualification.
Article 5 The source of funding for these Directives is government grants or the
University’s self-raised funds.
Article 6 Matters not addressed herein shall be handled in accordance with other
applicable regulations of the University or announcements by the
Center.
Article 7 The Directives shall be passed by the Committee, approved by the Vice
President for Academic Affairs, and then promulgated and
implemented. Any amendments shall be processed accordingly.

Article 1 National Chengchi University (NCCU or “the University”) formulates
the NCCU Directives for English Proficiency Test Rewards (“the
Directives”) to encourage students to improve their English proficiency
and participate in English proficiency tests.
Article 2 The recipient of the Directives are students of the University who hold
R.O.C nationality and are enrolled in the current semester (excluding
students enrolled in in-service programs and doctoral programs).
Article 3 Students who participate in English proficiency tests during their study
period and whose test results in listening, reading, speaking, and writing
all meet the standards of the University’s Table of English Proficiency
Tests and Corresponding Reward Levels (appendix), may be rewarded
according to the met standards.
Students shall apply during their study period, and each student may
receive the reward only once.

Students who take the BEST Test of English Proficiency (BESTEP) will
have their rewards processed and disbursed directly by the University
through a compiled list, with the caveat that rewards for the same
proficiency level are limited to once per person.
Article 4 First-year students who participate in and apply before the end of their
second semester, with results meeting the required standards in listening,
reading, speaking, and writing, may receive an additional NT$ 1,000 as a
Freshmen BESTEP English Proficiency Reward. The reward will be
processed and disbursed directly by the University through a compiled
list.
Article 5 The application documents for the rewards are as follows:
1. Application form for English Proficiency Test Rewards
2. Certificate or transcript of English proficiency test (The original
document will be returned after verification.)
3. If the name on the certificate or transcript is in English, please provide
additional documentation to verify the English name (e.g., passport).
Students shall obtain all the documents listed above at the time of
application.
Article 6 The application shall be processed according to the schedule and

submission procedures announced by Office of Academic Affairs each
semester.
Article 7 The rewards in the Directives are funded by the Ministry of Education’s
Program on Bilingual Education for Students in College (BEST), other
government subsidies or the University’s self-raised funds. The actual
reward amounts and quotas will be determined based on the annual
budget. In the event of budget interruptions or reductions, the University
reserves the right to suspend or reduce the scale of the rewards.

Multicultural Promotion Committee and submitted to the President of

text:
National Chengchi University Microprogram Regulations
Approved on June 6, 2022, during the second semester of the academic year 110, at the second
Academic Affairs Meeting.
Amendments to Articles 1, 2, 3, and 4 approved on June 5, 2023, during the second semester of
the academic year 111, at the second Academic Affairs Meeting.
Issued on August 17, 2023, as per Letter No. 1120025763.
Article 1 To enhance our students' competencies and promote systematic
learning, these regulations are established.
Article 2 Each teaching and research unit within the university may plan and
establish microprograms consisting of 8 to 12 credits. These can be
classified as "Introductory Microprograms" or "Advanced
Microprograms" based on the combination or characteristics of the
course.
Microprogram courses may include foundational, core, advanced, or
applied stages, primarily focusing on professional courses. However,
the foundational stage of "Introductory Microprograms" may be
designed as a general education course, limited to one course.
Article 3 Units planning to establish microprograms must clearly define the
program name, objectives, course structure, required subjects, and
credits, along with other relevant regulations. These plans must be
approved by the appropriate faculty-level meeting of the primary
course-offering unit and submitted to the Office of Academic Affairs
for record.
Article 4 Microprograms are managed by their respective teaching and research
units. Students who complete the required subjects and credits with
passing grades may apply for a completion certificate from the unit
that established the microprogram.
Article 5 Microprogram courses, except for repeated courses that require
approval from the student's major department, shall count towards
graduation credits by their respective colleges, departments, or
institutes. Graduate students (Master's and Ph.D. students) taking
undergraduate courses will not have those credits and grades included
in the calculation of semester or graduation grades.
Article 6 Students who previously studied in microprogram-setting units but did
not qualify and later re-enroll may, with approval from the setting
unit, apply for credit transfer, provided they have completed at least

one course in the microprogram.
Article 7 Undergraduate students enrolled in microprograms are not charged
credit fees. Graduate and doctoral students, as well as undergraduates
who delay graduation, shall pay credit fees and related expenses
according to the current academic year's tuition and fee standards of
the university.
Article 8 Students who have met the graduation requirements of their original
department or institute but have not completed the required subjects
and credits of the microprogram are not permitted to extend their
period of study.
Article 9 Any matters not covered in these regulations shall be handled in
accordance with the university's regulations and relevant laws.
Article 10 These regulations, upon approval by the Academic Affairs Meeting,
shall be promulgated and implemented by the President. The same
procedure applies to any amendments.

title: law14b.pdf

NATIONAL CHENGCHI UNIVERSITY
Guidelines for the Expansion of Minor Program Offerings
October 8, 2003 Approved by the 585th Administrative Meeting
August 1, 2018 Amended and approved by the 676th Administrative Meeting for Article 3
November 6, 2018 Promulgated under Document No. 1070034286
Article 1 National Chengchi University (NCCU or "the University") establishes these
guidelines to encourage all academic units to expand their minor program offerings,
providing students with diverse learning opportunities and enhancing their overall
competitiveness.
Article 2 Course Establishment
1) Minor program classes are typically formed with a minimum of 20 students
per class.
2) If the required number of students is not met, academic units may reallocate
their operational funds based on a self-sustaining principle. If redistribution
is not possible, the course will be canceled, and the academic unit must
arrange for students in the minor program to audit regular classes instead.
Auditing students are exempt from additional credit fees.
3) Students auditing regular classes as part of the minor program are not
required to pay additional credit fees. However, if the academic unit has
already established a dedicated minor program and a student, for other
reasons, cannot attend the dedicated program and must audit a general class,
the student must pay the credit fees.
4) After the adding or dropping courses period concludes, the Instruction
Resource, Office of Academic Affairs will notify academic units of minor
program courses with fewer than 20 enrolled students. The academic units
must confirm whether to cancel or continue offering such courses.
Article 3 Appointment of Minor Program Instructors
1) Academic units may hire adjunct instructors via written appointment.
2) Appointments must be approved through the University's three-tier review
process before courses are offered. If enrollment is insufficient and a course
is canceled, the instructor's qualification will be retained for future use when
the course is offered again.
3) The appointment, certification, and reappointment of adjunct instructors shall
be handled in accordance with the University's guidelines for employing
adjunct instructors.
4) Instructors hired under these guidelines are limited to teaching courses in the

minor program.
5) Adjunct instructors proposed by academic units must be identified as such in
the hiring documentation and will not be counted toward the unit's staffing
quota.
6) Academic units may propose slightly more adjunct instructors than required
to allow flexibility in managing the supply and demand for minor programs.
7) Adjunct instructors, like all teaching staff, may be rehired or not reappointed
depending on teaching needs.
8) Candidates for adjunct instructor positions may include doctoral candidates
of the University or professionals with a master's degree or higher.
9) Adjunct instructors are paid hourly using the credit fees collected, rather than
through the University's personnel budget.
Article 4 Maintenance of Teaching Quality
1) Course Evaluation Survey must be conducted for all minor program classes.
2) Full-time faculty members may teach minor program classes alongside
adjunct instructors.
Article 5 Financial Management
1) Programs offering specialized classes will collect credit fees from students in
accordance with regulations. Courses with practicums may charge additional
fees to hire teaching assistants. Practicum fees will be calculated at NT$250
per hour of practicum instruction.
2) Credit fees must be used exclusively for program-related purposes. In
addition to paying instructors’ hourly wages, the remaining funds should
primarily support the related academic units and administrative functions to
compensate for increased workloads.
3) If enrollment is insufficient to cover administrative support fees, such fees
will not be provided. If funds are inadequate to cover instructors’ hourly
wages, the class will not be offered.
4) The cost distribution ratio for administrative and academic units'
management fees will be determined separately.
Article 6 Implementation and Amendments
The Regulations shall be passed by the Administrative Meeting, and then
promulgated and implemented by the President. Any amendments shall be processed
accordingly.

National Chengchi University Regulations for Interscholastic Course
Selection in Taiwan
Approved by the Academic Affairs Meeting on Jun 14, 1996
Amended and approved by the Academic Affairs Meeting on Jan 7, 2002
Approved for future reference by the Ministry of Education in letter Tai (91) Kao Tze 91018828 on Feb 8, 2002
Amended and approved by the Academic Affairs Meeting on Dec 28, 2009
Approved for future reference by the Ministry of Education in letter Tai Kao Tze 0990049394 on Apr 7, 2010
Issued by Letter No. Cheng Jiao Zih 0990008212 on Apr 15, 2010
Amended and approved by the Academic Affairs Meeting on Jun 7, 2021
Approved for future reference by the Ministry of Education in letter Tai Chiao Kao 1100087167 on Jul 19, 2021
Issued by Letter No. Cheng Jiao Zih 1100021217 on Jul 28, 2021
Article 1. The National Chengchi University Regulations for Cross-campus Course Selection in Taiwan (hereinafter
referred to as the "Regulations") are established by National Chengchi University (NCCU) in accordance
with the University Act, the enforcement rules of the University Act, and NCCU regulations.
Article 2. NCCU students selecting courses offered by other universities shall seek approval from the relevant
department or college.
Students from other universities selecting NCCU courses shall seek the consent of their university, the
instructor of the course in NCCU, and the department or college offering the course in order to take the
courses.
Article 3. NCCU students selecting courses offered by other universities may be allowed to do so based on the
premise that NCCU does not offer the course selected in the specific semester.
NCCU students may select a maximum of 6 credits per semester. Those pursuing a double major, minor
degree, teacher training program, or with other special reason may be exempted from the aforesaid
maximum credit limit upon application on an individual basis.
Departments and institutes may set their own limits on the number of credits that students are allowed to
select via interscholastic courses throughout the semester and other relevant rules in addition to those
under these Regulations.
NCCU students selecting interscholastic courses shall pay the credit fee in accordance with the
regulations of the respective university. Students taking courses in partner universities shall follow the
terms of the collaboration agreement. For relevant regulations, please refer to NCCU's list of tuition fees.
Article 4. Students from other universities selecting NCCU courses shall pay the credit fee in accordance with the
regulations; students shall also pay the internship fee for selected courses that include an internship.
NCCU's regulations on credit fee payment are as follows:
1. Undergraduate course credit fees shall be charged in accordance with the charging regulations of
the department or college offering the course. Postgraduate course credit fees shall be charged in
accordance with the payment regulations of the department or college offering the postgraduate
course.

2. International students (including Chinese students) taking NCCU's general courses or courses
priced at a special level (such as teacher training courses) shall be charged twice the amount of the
original credit fee.
3. Credit fees for courses priced at a special level, such as those from on-the-job master programs,
shall be charged in accordance with the payment regulations of the specific program.
4. For zero-credit courses, a credit fee shall be charged according to the number of weekly course
hours.
5. For courses offered by partner universities, the terms of the collaboration agreement shall be
followed.
After completion of course selection, applications for dropping of courses and refund shall not be
accepted unless the course is canceled due to low enrollment.
Article 5. Students selecting interscholastic courses should fill in required particulars in the interscholastic course
selection system and print out the application form. The form should be submitted to the Registration
Section of the Office of Academic Affairs within the stipulated course selection period of the specific
semester to complete the course selection procedure. Applications noncompliant with the regulations or
submitted past the deadline shall be regarded as null.
Article 6. Course selection, fee payment, class attendance, issuance of grades, and so forth shall be conducted
according to the regulations of the university NCCU students select the courses from.
Course selection, fee payment, class attendance, issuance of grades, and so forth shall be conducted
according to NCCU regulations for students from other universities selecting NCCU courses. Upon the
conclusion of each semester, the Office of Academic Affairs shall forward the academic transcripts of the
interscholastic courses to the university students are enrolled in.
Article 7. These regulations and any amendments shall be approved by the Academic Affairs Meeting, shall be
submitted to the Ministry of Education for reference, and become effective after promulgation by the
President.

National Chengchi University Teaching Improvement Experimental
Program Regulations
February 10, 2009 Approved by the President
March 30, 2020 Amended and passed by the 1st Academic Affairs
Meeting, spring semester, Academic Year 2019-20
May 11, 2020 Promulgated via official letter Cheng Chiao Tzu No.
1090012001
October 18, 2021 Amended Articles 2, 3 passed by the 1st Academic
Affairs Meeting, fall semester, Academic Year 2021-22
November 9, 2021 Promulgated via official letter Cheng Chiao Tzu No.
1100033284
October 16, 2023 Amended Articles 3, 4 passed by the 1st Academic
Affairs Meeting, fall semester, Academic Year 2023-24
December 1, 2023 Promulgated via official letter Cheng Chiao Tzu No.
1120039460
Article 1 National Chengchi University (NCCU or “the University”) formulates
the NCCU Teaching Improvement Experimental Program Regulations to
encourage faculty to actively engage in teaching refinement and
innovation to enhance teaching quality and promote high quality
learning.
Article 2 All faculty members of this University, including part-time instructors
and above, are eligible to apply. Each person is allowed to submit one
application per semester as a principle, and a new proposal can only be
submitted after the completion of the previous one.
Article 3 The Center for Teaching and Learning Development ("the Center")
under the Office of Academic Affairs is responsible for processing
applications for the program, with the following related matters:
1. Application Courses: Limited to undergraduate courses.
2. Application Period: Submissions must be made within the
announced period at the end of each semester, and the
review results will be announced before the start of the new

semester.
3. Proposal Explanation: Application for this program is for
single course in a single semester. Applicants must submit
an application for the Teaching Improvement Experimental
Program within the specified time.
4. Proposal Content Includes: the motivation behind the research
project, research themes and objectives, literature review,
instructional design and planning, research design and execution
planning, expected tasks and outcomes, references, and other
relevant details.
Article 4 Review-related matters of the program
1. Review Procedure: The review committee is chaired by the Vice
President for Academic Affairs as the convener, with the Director of
the General Education Center and the Director of the Center as ex-
officio members. Three external scholars or experts may be invited
to assist with the review. The subsidies will be based on the number
of applications and the financial situation.
2. Review Criteria are as follows:
1) The degree of teaching refinement or innovation.
2) The coherence among elements of instructional design.
3) Expected outcomes.
4) The execution status of previous projects.

5) The use of digital learning to support instruction.
Article 5 Funding related matters
1. Operating Expenses: Up to NT$10,000 per course for teaching-
related operating expenses.
2. Personnel Expenses: Subsidy for one teaching assistant per
course. The assistant's salary shall not be lower than NT$6,000
per month, with the hourly wage not falling below the basic wage
announced by the Ministry of Labor.
3. Funding support comes from government subsidies or the
University's self-raised funds.
Article 6 Teachers who receive subsidies must complete the project as
scheduled, participate in the outcome presentation activities
organized by the Center, and submit financial reports and outcome
reports within the specified time.
Article 7 The responsibilities and obligations of the teaching assistants are
governed by Article 8, (2), (3), and (4) of the University’s Office of
Academic Affairs Teaching Assistant Funding Subsidy Directives.
Article 8 The Regulations shall be passed by the Academic Affairs Meeting and
then promulgated and implemented. Any amendments shall be
processed accordingly.

Affairs Meeting, fall semester, Academic Year
2023-24
January 11, 2024 Promulgated via official letter Cheng Chiao Tzu
No. 1130000849
Article 1 The Center for Teaching and Learning Development (“the Center”) under
National Chengchi University (NCCU or “the University”) Office of
Academic Affairs, formulates the NCCU Regulations for the
Implementation of Teacher Mentoring Program to establish an excellent
academic succession system.
Article 2 The mentorship team consists of a "Mentor" and a "Mentee."
Article 3 A Mentor must be a full-time faculty member of the University meeting
one of the following conditions:
1. Full-time professor of the University (including jointly appointed
professor).
2. Distinguished or Honorary Professor of the University.
3. Faculty member (including jointly appointed member) who has
received the "Ministry of Education Chair Professorship," "Ministry

of Education Academic Award," "National Science and Technology
Council Outstanding Research Award," or the University's
"Teaching Excellence Award", "Research Excellence Award" or
“Outstanding Teaching Award”.
Article 4 A Mentee must be an assistant professor or below of the University, who
has not yet been promoted in accordance with the "New Faculty
Promotion Regulations." Each eligible faculty member may apply for one
mentor to form a mentorship team. Participation in New Faculty
Orientation organized by the Center and other teaching enhancement
related activities will also be considered as reference for determining
qualifications.
Priority for mentee applications:
1. New assistant professor of the current year.
2. Assistant professor who joined within the last three years.
3. New associate professor of the current year.
4. Associate professor who joined within the last three years.
Article 5 Application period and process are as follows:
1. Applications are processed twice a year, in March and September
respectively.
2. Mentors can form a mentorship team with one to three mentees based
on their willingness. The application is submitted by the mentee.
3. Required documents for application:
1) Mentee application form.

2) Mentor profile form.
3) Mentorship activity planning form.
Article 6 The official duration of mentorship team activities is as follows:
1. March applicants: March to November.
2. September applicants: September to May of the following year.
Article 7 Mentorship team activities include individual and group activities, focusing
on the exchange of teaching, research, and service experiences. Individual
activity schedules are agreed upon by the mentor and mentee at the
beginning of the activity, with the principle of meeting and discussing once a
month. Group activities are organized by the Center for Teaching and
Learning Development, including various seminars, workshops, and related
events. All mentors and mentees are expected to participate to enhance team
bonding and experience sharing.
Article 8 To facilitate the smooth operation of mentorship activities, a subsidy of up to
NTD 20,000 per team per year is provided, subject to the Center's review and
adjustment.
Article 9 The subsidies stipulated in the regulations are funded by the University's
self-raised funds or government subsidies.
Article 10 The regulations shall be passed by the Academic Affairs Meeting and
submitted to the President of the University for approval, and then
promulgated and implemented. Any amendments shall be processed
accordingly.

NATIONAL CHENGCHI UNIVERSITY
Regulations for the Establishment of Thesis and Dissertation Awards
November 16, 2020 Amended and passed by the 211th University Council
Meeting
February 8, 2021 Promulgated via official letter Cheng Chiao Tzu No.
1100003350
January 12, 2024 Amended in full and passed by the 227th University
Council Meeting
February 1, 2024 Promulgated via official letter Cheng Chiao Tzu No.
1130003423
Article 1 National Chengchi University (NCCU or “the University”) formulates
the NCCU Regulations for the Establishment of Thesis and Dissertation
Awards (“the Regulations”) to oversee the establishment of the Thesis
and Dissertation Awards (“the Awards”) in order to recognize thesis
and dissertation authors with academic contributions and research
potential, along with their advisors.
Article 2 The recipients of the Awards are doctoral and master’s graduates who
obtained their degrees from the University within the two academic
years prior to the announcement of nominations, as well as their
advisors.
The Awards are granted once each academic year, with the number of
awards, in principle, based on 50 percent of the total recommendations
from the colleges. Master’s theses and doctoral dissertations are
calculated separately, and the Awards may remain unfilled. Relevant
schedule shall be managed in accordance with the announcement from
the Office of Academic Affairs.
Article 3 To evaluate the nominated theses and dissertations, the University shall
establish the Thesis and Dissertation Awards Selection Committee (“the
Committee”) consisting of eleven to thirteen members. The President,

Executive Vice President for Administrative Affairs, Vice President for
Academic Affairs, and Vice President for Research and Development
shall serve as ex-officio members, with the President serving as the
convener. The remaining committee members shall be recommended by
each college, with one to two experts or scholars from relevant fields,
either within or outside the University. The President shall appoint
seven to nine members to serve for a term of one year.
The Committee meeting requires the attendance of at least two-thirds of
the appointed members to proceed, and decisions shall be made with the
consent of two-third of those present.
Article 4 The recipients of the Awards may be recommended by the advisors or
degree examination committee members to each college; each college
shall establish relevant college-level regulations for the review of these
recommendations.
Each college’s nomination shall include the following documents:
1. Recommendation letter.
2. Nomination form (including relevant review materials).
3. Electronic file of the nominated thesis or dissertation.
4. College-level review regulations and related meeting records files.
The recommendation letter and nomination form shall detail the
justification for the Award, including the academic contributions and
research potential of the thesis or dissertation.
Article 5 The review procedure for the Awards is as follows:
1. Each college shall convene a review committee meeting in
accordance with its review regulations for the initial review.

External reviewers shall be invited to conduct substantive reviews
of dissertations.
2. Each college shall submit the results of the review and
recommendations to the Committee for final review. The
recommended quota is limited to one doctoral candidate and two
master's candidates; however, if there are more than ten doctoral
graduates from a college in the current academic year, one
additional doctoral candidate may be recommended.
3. The Committee shall conduct the final review and determine the
list of awardees based on the fairness of the award lists and the
ranking of recommendations from each college.
Article 6 To ensure that the theses and dissertations nominated by each college
are subject to public evaluation, the electronic full text of the nominated
theses and dissertations shall be made publicly available at the time of
recommendation.
Article 7 For the Thesis Award, each awardee shall receive a certificate and a
cash prize of NT$30,000, with their advisors receiving a certificate and
a cash prize of NT$10,000.
For the Dissertation Award, each awardee shall receive a certificate and
a cash prize of NT$50,000, with their advisors receiving a certificate
and a cash prize of NT$20,000.
In the event that a thesis or dissertation with multiple advisors is
awarded, the cash prize shall be distributed equally among the advisors.
The Awards shall be presented at a public ceremony.
Article 8 If the awarded theses or dissertation is found, in the accordance with the

University’s Guidelines for Review of Violations of Academic Ethics, to
involve plagiarism, forgery, copyright infringement, or other violations
of academic research ethics, the award shall be revoked. The certificate
and cash prize received by both the awardee and the advisor shall be
reclaimed.
Article 9 The Awards in the Regulations are funded by the University’s self-
raised funds and other government subsidies. The number of awardees
may be adjusted based on the allocated budget, or the implementation
of the Regulations may be suspended.
Article 10 The Regulations shall be passed by the University Endowment Fund
Management Committee and the University Council Meeting, and then
promulgated and implemented. Any amendments shall be processed
accordingly.

Article 1 National Chengchi University (NCCU or “the University”) formulates the
NCCU Directives for Subsidies to Encourage Faculty in Developing English as
a Medium of Instruction (EMI) Courses (“the Directives”) to enhance students’
English proficiency and international competitiveness, to foster an English-
medium teaching and learning environment, and to encourage faculty to offer
courses using English as a medium of instruction.
Article 2 The term “English as a Medium of Instruction (EMI) courses” referred to in the
Directives shall be courses in which teaching materials, instruction, interaction,
discussion, grading, and presentation of course outcomes are all conducted in
English. However, other languages may be used under specific circumstances,

such as group discussions or explanations of professional terms and complex
concepts.
General language courses (including relevant professional courses that should
be taught in English), courses for in-service program, courses that are self-
funded by credit fees, or courses that have received other subsidies are ineligible
for application.
Article 3 The subsidies and related matters for EMI courses at the University are
managed by the EMI Program Working Group Meetings, chaired by the
Executive Director of the Bilingual Education and Multicultural Promotion
Office (BMO).
Article 4 Full-time faculty of the University that offer EMI courses may be granted
subsidies.
Co-offered EMI courses (intra-college, cross-college, or cross-degree-level)
shall be subsidized only once. If an EMI course meets the criteria for both
distance learning and the subsidies in the Directives, it shall only choose one
type of subsidy.
EMI courses applied for the subsidies shall have at least one enrolling student
from the University. Priority for teaching assistant subsidy is given to
Article 5 EMI courses subsidized under the Directives are primarily for three-credit

courses. Subsidies for course material development shall be granted based on
the following principles:
1. For three-credit EMI courses, a subsidy of NT$ 6,000 is granted.
2. For two-credit EMI courses, a subsidy of NT$ 3,000 is granted.
3. For one-credit EMI courses, a subsidy of NT$ 1,500 is granted.
4. For newly established EMI courses, a subsidy of NT$ 10,000 is granted for
undergraduate course, and NT$ 5,000 for master’s and doctoral courses.
5. For continuing EMI courses, a subsidy of NT$ 1,500 is granted regardless
of the degree levels.
6. EMI courses with more than 40 domestic students or more than 10
international students enrolled shall be prioritized for subsidies for course
operational expense.
If an EMI course is co-taught by two or more faculties, the subsidy will be given
based on the percentage of lecture hours.
The amount of subsidies for course material development may be adjusted by
the Committee based on the annual budget allocation.
Article 6 The applying units for these subsidies shall be the colleges or other course-
offering units. The applying units shall submit the application in accordance
with the schedule and related materials announced by the Office of Academic

Affairs.
Article 7 Faculties receiving subsidies shall participate and share their teaching
reflections in EMI teaching experience exchange sessions, workshops, or course
observation activities organized by the University’s BMO or Center for
Teaching and Learning Development (CTLD).
Article 8 The subsidies stipulated in the Directives are funded by the Ministry of
Education’s Program on Bilingual Education for Students in College (BEST),
other government subsidies, or the University’s self-raised funds. The actual
subsidy amounts and quotas will be determined based on the annual budget. In
the event of budget interruptions or reductions, the University reserves the
right to suspend or reduce the scale of the subsidies.
Article 9 The Directives shall be passed by the Bilingual Education and Multicultural
Promotion Committee, submitted to the President for approval, and then
promulgated and implemented. Any amendments shall be processed
accordingly.

NATIONAL CHENGCHI UNIVERSITY
National Language Course Subsidy Regulations
March 21, 2022 Pass by the 1st Academic Affairs Meeting, Spring Semester, Academic Year 2021-2022
May 2, 2022 Promulgated via official letter Cheng Chiao Tzu No. 1110012273
Article 1 National Chengchi University (NCCU or "the University") formulates the NCCU National
Language Course Subsidy Regulations to promote the inheritance, revitalization, and
development of national languages, and to encourage faculty members at the University
to offer courses that contribute to the revitalization and development of national languages
facing a crisis of transmission.
Article 2 The term "national languages" as used in these regulations refers to the natural languages
used by various ethnic groups in Taiwan and Taiwan Sign Language.
Article 3 The national language courses covered by these Regulations include:
1. Courses focused on language instruction in national languages.
2. Professional or general education courses conducted in national languages.
Article 4 The University establishes the National Language Course Subsidy Review Committee (the
“Committee”), with the Vice President for Academic Affairs serving as an ex officio
member and convener. The Committee shall consist of five to nine members, with
additional members recommended by the Vice President for Academic Affairs from among
internal and external scholars and experts. The term of office for members is two years. A
student representative, recommended by the Student Association, shall also be appointed
for a one-year term. Members may be reappointed upon the expiration of their term. The
Committee is responsible for allocating subsidy funds and handling other related matters
in accordance with these regulations.
Article 5 Instructors of national language courses can apply for funding based on the type of
course:
1. Teaching Awards
1） New national language instruction courses: NT$10,000 per course per
semester; continuing courses: NT$6,000 per course per semester. If a course is
co-taught, the subsidy will be distributed based on the proportion of teaching
hours.
2） New professional or general education courses taught in a national language:
NT$20,000 per course per semester; continuing courses: NT$12,000 per course
per semester. If a course is co-taught, the subsidy will be distributed based on
the proportion of teaching hours.
2. Teaching Material Subsidies
1） New language instruction courses: NT$5,000 per course per semester for
teaching materials; continuing courses: NT$3,000 per course per semester.
2） New professional or general education courses taught in a national language:
NT$10,000 per course per semester for teaching materials; continuing courses:
NT$6,000 per course per semester.
Funds for teaching materials must be used exclusively for the designated course and

cannot be redirected for other purposes. All expenses must be documented and submitted
by the specified deadline, following the University's procedures and regulations. Unspent
funds generally cannot be carried over to the next fiscal year unless under special
circumstances. If a subsidized course is canceled, any disbursed funds must be returned.
Courses already receiving other project subsidies within the same fiscal year are not
eligible for these subsidies.
Article 6 Applications for these subsidies are processed once per semester for courses to be taught
in the following semester. Instructors wishing to apply must submit the following
documents:
1. National Language Course Subsidy Application Form.
2. Course syllabus.
3. Justification for the course, including its necessity and expected educational
outcomes.
4. Any additional relevant documents that may aid in the review process.
For continuing courses, past teaching outcomes and student feedback must also be
provided for the review.
Article 7 Funding for these subsidies will come from government grants or the University's own
revenue.
Article 8 The Regulations shall be passed by the Academic Affairs Meeting, and then promulgated
and implemented by the President. Any amendments shall be processed accordingly.

Article 1 National Chengchi University (NCCU or “the University”) formulates
the NCCU Directives for Rewards to Encourage Students to Enroll in
English as a Medium of Instruction (EMI) Courses (“the Directives”) to
enhance students’ English proficiency and international competitiveness,
to foster an English-medium teaching and learning environment, and to
encourage students to enroll in English as a medium of instruction
courses.
Article 2 The recipient of the Directives are students of the University who hold
R.O.C nationality and are enrolled in the current semester (excluding
students enrolled in in-service programs and doctoral programs).
Article 3 The term “English as a Medium of Instruction (EMI) courses” referred

to in the Directives shall be courses in which teaching materials,
instruction, interaction, discussion, grading, and presentation of course
outcomes are all conducted in English. However, other languages may
be used under specific circumstances, such as group discussions or
explanations of professional terms and complex concepts.
Students who enroll in general language courses (including relevant
professional courses that should be taught in English), courses for in-
service program, or doctoral courses are ineligible for application.
Article 4 The rewards of the Directives are as follows:
1. Course Reward:
A. For first-year students who, by the end of the second semester,
have enrolled in at least one EMI course and have completed
the BEST Test of English Proficiency (BESTEP) in listening,
reading, speaking, and writing, a reward of NT$ 1,000 is
granted.
B. For second-year students and first-year Master’s student
whose credits from passed EMI courses, taken during the
academic year, constitute at least 20% of their total credits for
the academic year, a reward of NT$ 2,000 is granted.

2. Cumulative Course Reward: For undergraduate students who have
completed the required number of EMI course credits before
graduation, a cumulative course reward is granted according to the
following:
A. Upon completion of 16 EMI course credits, a reward of NT$
2,000 is granted.
B. Upon completion of 32 EMI course credits, a reward of NT$
4,000 is granted.
C. Upon completion of 64 or more EMI course credits, a reward
of NT$ 10,000 is granted.
This grant is restricted to a single application per individual.
Disbursements are calculated based on the highest tier of cumulative
credit. Duplicate claims or awards are prohibited.
Article 5 Regarding the Course Reward mentioned in the preceding Paragraph 1,
the Office of Academic Affairs shall compile a list of eligible students
each semester for disbursement.
The Cumulative Course Subsidy described in the preceding Paragraph 2
requires students to submit an application according to the schedule and
submission procedures announced by Office of Academic Affairs each

semester. The rewards and a Certificate of Study shall be disbursed after
the application is approved and announced.
Article 6 The rewards in the Directives are funded by the Ministry of Education’s
Program on Bilingual Education for Students in College (BEST), other
government subsidies or the University’s self-raised funds. The actual
reward amounts and quotas will be determined based on the annual
budget. In the event of budget interruptions or reductions, the University
reserves the right to suspend or reduce the scale of the rewards.
Article 7 The Directives shall be passed by the Bilingual Education and
Multicultural Promotion Committee and submitted to the President of
the University for approval, and then promulgated and implemented.
Any amendments shall be processed accordingly.

title: law41b.pdf
text:
NATIONAL CHENGCHI UNIVERSITY
Regulations for Course Implementation
January 6, 2005 Passed by the 132nd University Council
June 14, 2005 Amended Articles 4, 24, revoked Article7 and passed by the 134th University
Council
January 16, 2009 Amended Articles 6,8,11 and passed by the 152nd University Council
January 14, 2011 Amended Articles 15 and passed by the 162nd University Council
June 27, 2016 Amended in full and passed by the 189th University Council
July 28, 2016 Promulgated via official letter Cheng Chiao Tzu No.1050022014
June 25, 2021 Amended in full and passed by the 214th University Council
July 28, 2021 Promulgated via official letter Cheng Chiao Tzu No.1100020890
Chapter1 Legislative Purpose
Article1 National Chengchi University ("NCCU" or "the University") formulates the NCCU
Regulations for Course Implementation to standardize course arrangements and teaching,
enhance teaching quality, and safeguard students’ rights and interests.
Chapter2 Course Structure and Principles of Course Offering
Article2 The structure of all courses at NCCU shall be in accordance with the following
regulations:
1. The graduation credit requirement for the bachelor's degree is 128 credits, including
common compulsory credits, compulsory professional credits, and elective credits.
The credit distribution for each category is as follows:
1) General compulsory credits: Including general education courses and physical
education courses, the credits for general education courses are 28 credits, and
physical education courses are 4 credits, totaling 32 credits. Students admitted in
or before the 108th academic year, general education credits range from 28 to 32,
and physical education is zero-credit across four semesters.
2) Professional compulsory credits: The number of compulsory professional credits
for each bachelor's degree is determined by individual departments based on
professional considerations, and the ratio should be in accordance with the
provisions of Article 3, Paragraph 2 of the Course Streamlining Plan.
3) Undergraduate elective courses: Credits are selected by students from within or
outside their department, excluding repeated courses with identical names or inter-
institutional courses not recognized by the department.
2. Master’s and Doctoral Programs: Up to one-fourth of the total graduation credits may
be selected from (graduate) courses outside the student’s department or institute.
Exclusions apply to repeated courses with identical names or inter-institutional
courses not recognized by the department.
Article3 The principles and review mechanisms for course offerings at NCCU shall be handled
in accordance with the following regulations:
1. General education courses for undergraduates must be approved by the General
Education Center Committee and the Academic Affairs Meeting before being offered.
2. Departments shall draft lists of compulsory courses, which must be reviewed and
approved by the Curriculum Committee and the Academic Affairs Meeting. Courses
shall then be offered according to the approved lists.
3. Elective courses should be offered in proportion to the total elective credit
1

requirements of students in each department.
4. Distance learning courses must adhere to NCCU’s Digital Learning Regulations. To
provide students with comprehensive course information, the teaching syllabi for
courses must be reviewed and approved by the departmental affairs meeting or the
departmental curriculum committee before being published online. Starting from the
first semester of the 109th academic year, unapproved courses shall not be offered.
Article4 The number of courses offered in each program (undergraduate’s, master’s, doctoral)
shall be planned based on students’ graduation requirements.
Article5 Courses with 1, 2, or 3 credits are offered on a single semester basis; courses with 4, 6,
or 8 credits are offered on full academic year basis.
Article6 Courses with identical names, content, schedules, instructors, and credit hours may be
offered jointly., except in the following cases:
1. Undergraduate’s first- and second-year courses combined with master’s courses.
2. Doctoral courses combined with undergraduate's courses
3. In-service master’s program or extension education courses combined with general
academic courses.
Chapter3 Course Arrangement and Scheduling
Article7 Weekly classes shall be scheduled from Monday to Friday, between 8:00 AM and 9:00
PM. Exceptions include:
 Class Tutor Time and weekends, where no classes are scheduled.
 In-service master’s programs, which may be scheduled according to actual needs.
 Internship courses, which must specify class times in the timetable’s remarks section.
Article8 To optimize the use of classroom resources and prevent overly concentrated course
scheduling, departments shall distribute courses evenly across the week in accordance
with the scheduling principles outlined for each academic year.
Undergraduate courses shall be arranged based on the number of courses that can be
scheduled in each time slot, ensuring that general education course time slots do not
overlap with other undergraduate courses.
For courses not scheduled in compliance with the above provisions, the respective
departments shall be responsible for arranging the classrooms.
Article9 Faculty members shall teach according to the scheduled time, and each credit-hour
course must be taught for a full 18 weeks.
Article10 Full-time faculty in the general academic system may not concentrate their weekly
teaching hours into a single day. However, this restriction does not apply to those whose
weekly teaching hours are fewer than four. The general academic system does not
include in-service master’s programs.
Article11 Full-time faculty members in each department are required to offer undergraduate
courses every academic year. Exceptions apply to faculty members in independent
institutes or those who, under NCCU regulations, have their teaching reduced to one
course.
Article12 Full-time faculty members must teach at least three hours per week during the 18 weeks
of each semester.
Article13 For full-time faculty members whose total annual teaching hours exceed three hours,
their courses may not be completed within a single semester.
Article14 Course adjustments by NCCU course-offering units shall be handled as follows:
2

1. After submitting course schedules to the Instructional Resource Section, course-
offering units may handle additions, cancellations, changes in instructors, schedules,
classrooms, or other corrections within the specified period set by NCCU. However,
no changes to schedules, course additions, or cancellations may be made after the
course add/drop deadline.
2. Courses scheduled for the entire academic year may not be canceled or rescheduled
in the second semester.
3. Undergraduate and general education courses may not be arbitrarily canceled after
the initial course selection period unless enrollment is insufficient or special reasons
are approved through official documentation.
Article15 For departments with a single class, each course may only be offered once per academic
year, except for general education, interdisciplinary, and minor courses. For departments
with multiple classes, additional sections may be offered if enrollment justifies it. In
special circumstances, adjustments may be proposed to the Curriculum Committee and
Academic Affairs Meeting for approval.
Article16 Courses with specialized content may add additional sections upon approval by the
Curriculum Committee. However, if the reason for the additional section is no longer
applicable, the course should revert to a single section.
Article17 General education courses shall be offered as a single section for each subject by default.
If additional sections are needed, approval must be obtained from the General Education
Center Committee and the Academic Affairs Meeting before the courses can be offered.
Article18 The minimum enrollment standards for courses shall be as follows:
1. Minimum enrollment for each class:
1) Undergraduate courses: 7 students.
2) Master’s courses: 3 students. For master’s programs admitting fewer than 15
students, the minimum is 2 students.
3) Doctoral courses: 1 student.
4) Jointly offered master’s and doctoral courses: If no doctoral students enroll, the
course shall follow the standards for master’s courses.
2. After the course add/drop period, if the enrollment does not meet the above standards,
the course shall be canceled.
3. Courses with no NCCU students enrolled, and attended only by students from other
institutions, shall also be canceled.
Article19 Courses offered by full-time faculty members that do not meet the minimum enrollment
requirements may still proceed under the following conditions:
1. The course is recognized as a specialized subject by the NCCU Curriculum
Committee.
2. For year-long courses, if the first semester has already been completed, insufficient
enrollment in the second semester will not lead to cancellation.
Chapter4 Calculation of Faculty Teaching Hours
Article20 The calculation of teaching hours for faculty members shall adhere to the annual Course
Streamlining Plan and teaching load adjustment plan submitted by each college. These
calculations must comply with relevant Ministry of Education regulations and NCCU’s
faculty teaching hour and overtime pay calculation guidelines.
Article21 Teaching hours are calculated at one clock hour per credit hour. Exceptions to this rule
3

may be made under special circumstances with approval from the Curriculum
Committee and the Academic Affairs Meeting.
Article22 The minimum teaching load for full-time faculty members is 12 hours per academic year.
If individual colleges or departments set higher requirements, those requirements shall
take precedence.
 Each college or department may establish a flexible adjustment mechanism for
individual faculty members’ teaching loads within the total number of courses offered,
but no faculty member may teach fewer than 12 hours annually.
 The total teaching hours of full-time faculty members for courses outside the general
academic system must not exceed their teaching hours within the general academic
system.
 The term “general academic system” does not include in-service master’s programs.
Article23 Full-time faculty members holding administrative positions may have their teaching
loads reduced. Newly hired faculty members may also receive reduced teaching loads
during their first three academic years, with a maximum reduction of three hours per year.
However, any reduced teaching hours must be compensated by other full-time faculty
members within the same department or institute.
Article24 If the actual teaching hours of a full-time faculty member during an academic year fall
short of the teaching hours originally assigned by their college, it shall be considered a
deficiency in teaching hours and handled as follows:
1. Any deficiency in the first semester must be compensated in the second semester;
any deficiency in the current academic year must be compensated in the following
academic year.
2. Faculty members with insufficient teaching hours during any academic year shall not
be permitted to teach part-time outside the university or offer courses outside the
general academic system in the subsequent academic year.
3. Each unit may include cases of insufficient teaching hours as one of the necessary
conditions for eligibility for related awards or project funding applications.
4. Each college or department shall include cases of insufficient teaching hours in the
basic performance evaluations of faculty members and in the evaluation criteria for
teaching units.
5. If a department accumulates two consecutive academic years of insufficient teaching
hours among its faculty, no new faculty members may be hired for that department
until the issue is resolved. If the situation persists for three consecutive academic
years, the department’s faculty quota may be reduced.
The accumulation of deficiencies referenced in the previous item pertains to faculty
members within the same department and is not limited to individual faculty members.
Article25 In-service master’s programs may be exempt from the application of Articles 4, 7, 14,
and 19 of these regulations.
Article26 To align with the implementation of the Course Streamlining Plan, the Office of
Academic Affairs shall, by the end of each academic year, track and assess the execution
of evaluation metrics under the plan. Results shall be submitted to each teaching unit for
review and improvement, with responses forwarded to the Curriculum Committee and
the Academic Affairs Meeting for approval.
Article27 Matters not covered by these regulations shall be handled in accordance with relevant
4

provisions from the Ministry of Education and NCCU.
Chapter5 Supplementary Provisions
Article28 These regulations shall take effect upon approval by the University Council and be
promulgated and implemented by the President. Any amendments shall follow the same
procedure.
