title: law46b.pdf
text:
National Chengchi University Midterm and Final In-Class Examination Regulations
Approved on December 28, 1994, during the 1st Academic Semester of Academic Year 1994
Amended and approved on June 4, 2007, during the 2nd Academic Semester of Academic Year 2006
Amended and approved on October 20, 2008, during the 1st Academic Semester of Academic Year 2008
Amended and approved on June 1, 2015, during the 2nd Academic Semester of Academic Year 2014
Article 1 Midterm and final examinations each semester shall be held during the
original class hours and in the original classrooms as scheduled in the
academic calendar. Should the need arise, instructors may request large
examination venues from the Academic Affairs Section.
Article 2 Instructors may determine the dates for the midterm and final examinations
based on the progress of teaching or choose other methods to assess students'
grades. If the examination period is not during the original class period,
instructors should communicate thoroughly with students to avoid class or
exam scheduling conflicts.
Article 3 The date of the final in-class examination can be moved up one week,
provided that the actual number of teaching hours for the subject is not
reduced.
Article 4 Instructors who need to print exam questions should submit them to the
Academic Affairs Section for printing three days before the scheduled in
class examination of each subject.
Article 5 Instructors should personally or assign someone to collect the exam
questions and papers from the Academic Affairs Section prior to each in-
class examination.
Article 6 For in-class examinations of each subject, instructors shall discretionarily
handle student absences and make-up exams.
Article 7 After the completion of each subject's in-class examination, instructors are
responsible for collecting, reviewing, and archiving the exam papers, and
submitting the grades within the specified period.
Article 8 Students with disabilities holding a certification issued by the Ministry of
Health and Welfare or a special education student assessment certification
issued by the Ministry of Education with special examination needs may
apply for special examination arrangements at the Resource Room of the
Student Affairs Office's Physical and Mental Health Center. Upon approval,
instructors and related units shall provide the necessary assistance.
Article 9 These regulations shall be implemented after approval by the Academic
Affairs Meeting. The same applies to amendments.

title: law35b.pdf
text:
National Chengchi University
Guidelines for Setting up the Curriculum Committee
Approved by the 84th University Affairs Meeting on June 16, 1995.
Article 1, 2, 4, 6 and 8 were amended and approved by the 145th University Affairs Meeting, September 14, 2007.
Article 2 was amended and approved by the 152nd University Affairs Meeting on January 16, 2009.
Issued by Letter No. Cheng Jiao Zih 0980002000, February 24, 2009.
Article 2 was amended and approved by the 212nd University Affairs Meeting, January 15, 2021.
Issued by Letter No. Cheng Jiao Zih 1100004884, February 23, 2021.
Amended and approved by the 229th University Affairs Meeting, June 21, 2024.
Issued by Letter No. Cheng Jiao Zih 1130024334, July 23, 2024.
Article 1 These Guidelines accord with Article 24 of University Law and Article 8 of Organization
Rules of National Chengchi University (hereinafter referred to as 'NCCU').
Article 2 In order to plan and review the curriculum, the Curriculum Committee operates on three
levels. Apart from the university-level Curriculum Committee (hereinafter referred to as
'the Committee'), there should also be department-level committees in the Physical
Education Department and the colleges, whose establishment procedures must be
submitted for approval by the Committee and the Academic Affairs Council.
Departments, graduate institutes, and degree programs are required to establish their own
curriculum committees at the departmental level, with their establishment procedures
subject to approval by relevant college-level meetings.
Article 3 The Committee is comprised of 15-19 committee members and one convener, who is the
Director of Academic Affairs. The committee members are on-campus and off-campus
experts or scholars hired by the President of NCCU, representatives from industry and
two students.
Article 4 Duties of the Committee:
1. Reviewing compulsory courses of the university.
2. Reviewing compulsory professional courses offered by all departments and graduate
institutes.
3. Conducting research on how to improve the curriculum offered by all colleges,
departments and graduate institutes.
4. Conducting research on other issues relevant to the improvement of the curriculum.
A proposal may be submitted if it is endorsed by more than three representatives of the
Committee.
All proposals shall be submitted in written form to the curriculum division in the Office
of Academic Affairs 10 days before the convention of the Committee.
Article 5 The composition and responsibilities of college and department-level curriculum
committees shall be stipulated separately in their procedures of establishment. However,
each committee must include at least one student representative, and may also appoint
several scholars, experts from within or outside the university, or professionals from the
industry.
Article 6 The Committee is to be convened once every semester in principle and chaired by the
convener. Occasional meetings can be convened if deemed necessary.
Article 7 Members of the Committee are designated by the President of NCCU. The tenure of
student representatives is one year; other members hold the position for two years and
are eligible to resume the position once elected again.
Article 8 All the concluded matters in the Committee shall be reviewed by the Academic Affairs
Meeting.
Article 9 The Guidelines and any amendments will be promulgated upon approval by the
Academic Affairs Meeting of NCCU. The same procedures shall apply to any subsequent
amendments.

title: law39b.pdf
text:
NATIONAL CHENGCHI UNIVERSITY
Regulations for the Implementation of the Integrated Core
Curriculum
June 14, 2006 Approved at the First Interim Administrative Meeting of the 2005
Academic Year
October 2, 2013 Amended in full and passed by the 648th Administrative Meeting
August 5, 2015 Amended Articles 10 and passed by the 660th Administrative Meeting
Article 1 National Chengchi University (NCCU or “the University”) formulates the
guidelines to optimize the allocation and utilization of teaching resources for
core curriculum courses, provide students with greater flexibility in course
selection, and establish a standardized framework for academic units to offer
integrated core curriculum courses.
Article 2 The term "integrated core curriculum courses" as used in these guidelines
refers to core courses with similar titles and content. To achieve the benefits
of integration outlined in the preceding article, related academic units shall
plan and consolidate these courses according to the relevant provisions of
these guidelines and apply for course offerings. The scope of core
curriculum courses shall be determined by the NCCU’s Curriculum
Committee.
Article 3 The integration of core curriculum courses shall be initiated by the
responsible academic unit (“the Convening Unit"), which will form an
integration task force comprising representatives from related course-
offering units to draft and submit an integration plan.
In cases where disputes arise over the designation of the Convening Unit,
the matter shall be resolved through negotiation among the relevant course-
offering units. If an agreement cannot be reached, the following criteria
shall apply:
1.The total number of students enrolled in the subject course offered by
faculty members of the unit over the preceding four semesters.
2.The number of faculty members from the unit who taught the subject course
during the preceding four semesters.
Upon approval of the integration plan, the designated the Convening Unit shall
serve as the course-offering unit for the integrated core curriculum course and
will be responsible for all associated administrative tasks.

Article 4 The integration plan referenced in the preceding article shall include the
following:
1. Details of the courses offered before and after integration, including the
course-offering units, course titles, types, credit hours, instructors,
number of sections, enrollment numbers per section, class schedules, and
semesters offered.
2. A unified syllabus for the integrated course.
3. Operating guidelines for the integration task force.
Article 5 The offering of integrated core curriculum courses shall take into account
the following criteria:
1. Participation in the integration by at least two academic units that are
actively offering the course.
2. The total number of students enrolled in the course over the preceding
four semesters.
3. The number of academic units that designated the course as compulsory
courses over the preceding four semesters.
4. The benefits of integration, including meeting at least one of the
following thresholds for each semester:
1) Offering at least two sections with an average enrollment of over 50
students per section.
2) Offering a single section with an enrollment exceeding 120 students.
Article 6 Integrated core curriculum courses planned and consolidated in accordance
with Articles 3 to 5 must be approved by the NCCU’s Curriculum
Committee and the Academic Affairs Meeting before they can be offered.
For integrated courses already approved, continued offering does not
require additional review. Course-offering units may adjust the number of
sections as needed, provided they meet the enrollment thresholds specified
in Item 4 of the previous article.
The Curriculum Committee shall annually review the teaching effectiveness
of integrated courses based on the following criteria, which serve as a
reference for continued integration status:
1. The number of sections offered and enrollment figures per section.
2. Results from teaching evaluations.
3. Timely submission of course syllabi as required.
4. Uploading of teaching materials to the integrated course webpage.

Article 7 To provide students with greater flexibility in course selection, class
schedules for the same integrated core curriculum course must be
distributed across different time slots, excluding general education time
blocks.
Article 8 During the preliminary course selection phase, course-offering units for
integrated core curriculum courses may prioritize enrollment for students
from participating academic units (including students pursuing double
majors or minors) by pre-allocating slots. However, the number of
prioritized slots must not exceed 75% of the section’s capacity. Should this
threshold be exceeded, the Office of Academic Affairs will increase the
section capacity to reserve 25% of the slots for general university students.
During the add/drop period, all students shall have equal access to enroll.
Article 9 For integrated core curriculum courses with enrollment exceeding 70
students after the add/drop period, teaching hours per credit may be
increased by 0.1 for every 10 additional students (rounded up to the nearest
10). The maximum increase shall not exceed 1.5 times the actual teaching
hours.
Article 10 To ensure teaching quality and enhance the effectiveness of integrated core
curriculum courses, relevant university units shall provide the following
teaching support:
1. Priority allocation of teaching assistants, with instructors responsible for
their training.
2. Priority assignment of suitable classrooms.
3. Scheduling of after-class tutoring services through Center for Teaching
and Learning Development.
4. Establishment of an integrated course webpage by the course-offering
unit to provide syllabus, teaching schedules, self-learning platforms, and
related information.
5. Operational funding from the Office of Academic Affairs to support
webpage development, multimedia resources, supplementary teaching,
and the consolidation and uploading of teaching materials. Funding
standards and amounts will be determined based on the number of
sections offered, completion of teaching material uploads, and available
budget for the academic year.

Article 11 Matters not covered in these guidelines shall be handled in accordance
with relevant regulations and the resolutions of the Curriculum Committee
and Academic Affairs Meeting.
Article 12 The Directives shall be passed by the Academic Affairs Meeting, and then
promulgated and implemented by the President. Any amendments shall be
processed accordingly.

title: law75b.pdf
text:
Teachers' Guide to Mid-semester Leaves and Makeup Classes
Passed by the Academic Affairs Meeting in its 1st Meeting of the 2nd Semester of the 2013 Academic Year
Confirmed by the Academic Affairs Meeting in its 2nd Meeting of the 2nd Semester of the 2013 Academic Year
1. If lecturers have classes while on leave, but the reasons for taking the leave do not conflict
with the times of the classes, then they will teach the classes as usual and not be required
to schedule makeup classes. Potential scenarios include the following:
(1) It is the other lecturer's turn to teach a jointly offered course.
(2) The reason for taking the leave is to take the class on a course-related field trip,
such as a seminar or tour.
(3) The lecturer is able to finish a class while on leave before leaving the university or
start a class after returning to the university.
2. Lecturers who have classes while on leave but are unable to teach the classes should
schedule makeup classes based on the number of sessions. The number of makeup
sessions should be identical to the number of original sessions. Lecturers are advised not
to combine several classes into one makeup session. For example, it is not advised to teach
five 10-minute sessions between classes as one makeup class.
3. Lecturers who conduct interactive "remote teaching" via the Internet while on leave
should provide synchronous or nonsynchronous remote interaction. The content and
quantity of time should be equivalent to the original classes.
4. Lecturers who intend to find substitute lecturers or speakers during a leave of absence are
advised to comply with the following rules:
(1) When asking full-time/part-time lecturers at NCCU to serve as substitute lecturers,
ensure they are from sufficiently similar fields.
(2) When asking lecturers from other universities to serve as substitute lecturers,
ensure they are from sufficiently similar fields and hold similar positions.
(3) When inviting outside parties without lecturer qualifications to give speeches,
ensure there is a substitute lecturer in either of the two categories above present.
The field and position of a substitute lecturer in the preceding paragraph should be
described on the leave application.
5. Lecturers who are taking leaves and arrange for students to write examinations during the
time should ensure teaching assistants are present as proctors. If students are left to do
their homework, watch videos or conduct other self learning activities, teaching assistants
should be present to provide instructions or guidance. The teaching assistants should be
teaching assistants who are allocated by the NCCU teaching or administrative units, and
their names should be listed in the corresponding course outlines or leave applications.
The teaching assistants should possess adequate expertise and education levels (also to be
specified on the leave applications). In the absence of a teaching assistant, if students are
left alone to study on their own or conduct course related activities, the sessions should be
treated as homework from regular classes, and the lecturer will not be considered to have
provided a makeup class.

6. The total number of hours of makeup classes, substitution and teaching modes referred to
under Articles 2 to 5 for each course in each semester should not exceed three eighteenths
of the total number of required teaching hours (eighteen hours multiplied by the number of
credits) in a semester.
7. Any field trip while a lecturer is on leave should be led by the lecturer instead of a
teaching assistant, as field trips involve higher risks.
8. Any seminar or tour to be taken by students by themselves (especially when students will
be required to write reports afterward) while a lecturer is on leave, if unaccompanied by
the lecturer, should not be treated as a class or makeup class.
9. Lecturers should not end classes early or shorten courses. For example, lecturers should
not finish courses for graduating classes prematurely at the end of May, or finish general
courses in the 15th or 16th week, or shorten courses by adjusting their teaching speed. The
Ministry of Education stipulates eighteen teaching hours for each credit (except on
statutory holidays), including the time for examinations and learning assessments. In the
absence of examinations, other teaching activities should be arranged to actually deliver
classes or makeup classes.
10. Zero credit courses for which lecturers do not receive pay will be exempted from the rules
above.

title: law33b.pdf
text:
NATIONAL CHENGCHI UNIVERSITY
Regulations for Mobile Phone Use
January 7, 2002 Passed by the Academic Affairs Meeting
1. National Chengchi University (NCCU or “the University”) formulates the NCCU
Regulations for Mobile Phone Use to enhance teaching quality and maintain
campus order.
2. Instructors and students shall turn off mobile phones during classes held in
classrooms or sports venues to prevent disruptions to focused learning and
teaching activities.
3. During assemblies or gatherings, to maintain a quiet environment and ensure
smooth proceedings, instructors and students are required to turn off mobile
phones or switch them to silent mode when entering auditoriums or meeting
rooms.
4. For other campus locations not covered in the preceding clause, mobile phone
usage shall comply with the regulations set forth by the respective management
units.
5. If a student refuses to follow instructions, the teacher may confiscate the student’s
mobile phone and return it after class. In severe cases, the matter may be referred
to the National Chengchi University Student Award and Penalty Committee for
review.
6. The Regulations shall be passed by the Academic Affairs Meeting and then
promulgated and implemented. Any amendments shall be processed accordingly.

Article1 NationalChengchiUniversity(NCCUor“theUniversity”)formulatestheNCCUCourse
Evaluation Survey Regulations (“The Regulations”) in accordance with Article 5,
Paragraph 1 of the UniversityAct. The purpose is to elevate the quality of courses and
student learning outcomes, and to provide reference for faculty feedback and course
design.
Article2 The Regulations shall be applicable to all courses of the undergraduate programs,
master’s programs (including In-service Master’s Programs) and doctorate programs. It,
however, shall not apply to special programs such as sport teams, service programs and
ChineseLanguageprograms.Inspecialcases,exemptionfromparticipatingintheSurvey
maybegrantedto thePresident forapproval.
Article3 The questionnaires for the Course Evaluation Survey (“the Survey”) shall be developed
collectively by the Center for Teaching and Learning Development, the Office of
Institutional Research and the Instruction Resource Section, Office ofAcademicAffairs
after consulting the opinions of relevant scholars, experts, teachers, and students. The
questions shall beadoptedwhenapprovedbythe EvaluationCommitteeoftheNCCU.
All colleges or related academic units may design customized questions based on the
features of each course. The questions shall be agreed by the respective curriculum
committeesofthecollegeorotheracademicunitsandapprovedbythePresidentofNCCU
beforetheyaresubmittedtotheInstructionResourceSection,OfficeofAcademicAffairs.
Thecustomizedquestions shall not beincludedinscoring.
Article4 The Computer Center is responsible for the management of the Survey system and the
export of relevant data.The Instruction Resource Section, Office ofAcademicAffairs is
responsibleforthe announcement, implementation,andresult statistics oftheSurvey.
Article5 TheSurveys shall berespondedtoonline,includingmid-term surveys and final surveys.
Inprinciple,mid-termsurveysshallbeconductedoneweekbeforetheweekofmid-term
examinationofeachsemester.Finalsurveysshallbeconductedbetweenthe15thandthe
17th week of each semester. The schedule for each semester shall be announced by the
Office of Academic Affairs. The relevant academic units and teachers shall notify the
students tocompletethequestionnaires online.
Article6 The results of mid-term survey are provided for the faculty as a reference for course
adjustment.
The final survey shall include two parts, the Course Evaluation Survey and the Core

Competency Self-Assessment. The results of the Course Evaluation Survey shall be
scored.
Theresultsofthefinalsurveyshallbesenttotherespectiveunitsasareferenceforfaculty
performanceevaluation,promotion,selectionofoutstandingteachingstaffandthecourse
subsidies.
Incasethefinalsurveyresultoffull-timefacultyofNCCUmeetstheconditionssetforth
in Article 4, Subparagraph 5 of “ National Chengchi University Faculty Basic
Performance Evaluation Regulations” and Article 6, Subparagraph 5 of “National
Chengchi University Faculty Performance Evaluation Regulations”, the Instruction
ResourceSection,OfficeofAcademicAffairsshallprovidealistoffacultytotheheadof
the responsible unit and Center for Teaching and Learning Development for early
awareness and assistance inimprovement.
Article7 Uponcompletingthestatisticsofthefinalsurveyresults,theInstructionResourceSection,
Office ofAcademicAffairs shall announce the average scores of the Course Evaluation
Surveyforeachacademicunit ontheOfficeofAcademicAffairs website.
The results of the Survey for each subject will be available to faculty after they submit
thefinal grades forthe entireclass.
The heads of the academic units may access the survey results of faculty under their
supervisionafterthedeadlineforgradesubmission.
Article8 Duringtheperiodofcourseselection,thestudentsmayinquireonthefinalsurveyresults
of the course instructor for the latest six semesters. The inquiry, however, is available to
the undergraduate programs only. The information provided includes the score of each
course(whenthetotalscoreisover60),thenumberofstudentsenrolled,textualfeedback
andresponse rate.
Article9 Students who have completed the final survey for the semester are entitled to receive
bonus points based on the rules set forth in theAppendix, which may be added to their
cumulativepoints intheprocess ofinitial courseselectionforthenext semester.
The aforementioned bonus points received in the survey process shall only be valid for
the subsequent semester.The points will not be preserved if the student applies for leave
ofabsenceorretainment ofstudent status inthenext semester.
Article10 All personnel involved in the Survey process shall carefully follow the confidentiality
requirements.
Article11 TheRegulationsshallbepassedbytheAcademicAffairsMeeting,andthenpromulgated
andimplemented.Any amendments shall beprocessedaccordingly.

Appendix: Other departmental policies
I Life Guidance and Overseas Chinese Student Advising Section (LGOCSAS) – Administration Building, 3rd Floor
1. Policy for tuition refunds when requesting a leave of absence / terminating studies (Contact: 02-29393091 ext. 62226)
（1）Before the deadline to pay tuition, currently enrolled students who request a leave of absence or termination of studies do not need to pay the
additional school fees. Newly enrolled students that request a leave of absence or termination of studies need to bring their First Commercial
Bank or Taiwan Post account information to the Cashier Section so that they can wire the refund into the right account. Apart from inquiries
about tuition refunds, other questions about the procedures for leaves of absence and terminating studies can be directed to the Admissions
Section of the Office of Academic Affairs at extension 63279. Students who had assigned a bed should go to the Student Housing Service
Section to complete the refund process.
（2）When requesting a leave of absence or terminating studies, LGOCSAS is responsible for starting the refund process. The Cashier Section then
transfers the refund directly into your account. Students should not go to LGOCSAS to process their refund.
（3）Students that complete the process for leave of absence or termination of studies before the deadline for paying tuition will receive a full refund
of the additional school fees. Students that complete the process for leave of absence or termination of studies one day after the deadline for
paying tuition, up to the day that marks completion of one-third the term, will be refunded two-thirds of the additional school fees. Students
that complete the process for leave of absence or termination of studies one day after the marks one-third completion of the term up to the day
that marks completion of two-third the term will be refunded one-thirds of the additional school fees. Students that request a leave of absence
or termination of studies after the day that marks completion of two-third the semester are not refunded additional school fees (no exceptions).
2. Overseas Chinese students please contact the LGOCSAS - Administration Building, 3rd Floor(Contact: 02-29393091 ext. 63011、63013)
（1）Overseas Chinese students enrolled at NCCU should take note of the following: any overseas Chinese student that does not apply for an
overseas Chinese visa before the deadline, does not register an address or change of address before the deadline, overstays his/her visa, or does
not carry his/her passport or ARC at all times will be dealt with according to the Immigration Law. Students should pay special attention to
issues that concern their vital interests as alien residents in Taiwan.
（2）After reading this notice overseas Chinese students with a Taiwan ID should bring a copy of the ID to LGOCSAS before enrolling for classes to
confirm their status.
II Student Housing Service Section –Administration Building, 3rd Floor
1. Dormitory Regulations (Contact: 02-29393091 ext. 63252)
（1） Undergraduate students are limited to a dorm stay of one academic year (ending on the first day of the summer vacation term). When your stay
is up you will need to re-apply for the dorms. Graduate students are limited to a dorm stay of four semesters. Ph.D. students are limited to a
dorm stay of eight semesters. Counting begins with the semester when you are approved to live in the dorms. Graduate students may not
re-apply for the dorms once they reach the maximum duration of stay.
（2）Dormitory move-in date:
Currently enrolled undergraduate students are scheduled to move in on 23 August 2025.The move-in information will be published on website.
（3）Enrolled students with a dorm assignment who wish to cancel their assignment or move out of the dorms should fill out the dorm cancellation
form (download from the Student Housing Service Section website) . The refund policy is based on the regulations set down by the Student
Housing Service Section. Please request your cancellation as early as possible so that students on the waiting list can be assigned a dorm bed
promptly. You will receive only a partial refund of the dorm fee if your cancellation is received after the deadline.
（4）Students who have come to the end of the dorm semester limits, or those who want to cancel their dorm application for the following semester,
must follow the procedures set by the regulations in the NCCU Dormitory Counseling and Management Policy and the NCCU Residence Hall
Deposit Policy, so that the tuition bill for next semester can be updated and the dorm fee/deposit can be refunded. If you do not submit a
request to move out of the dorms according to these regulations, the deposit will not be refunded.
（5）New undergraduate and graduate dorm residents are required to attend the fire prevention workshop. Students that fail to attend the workshop
will be given 8-10 penalty points in accordance with to the Dormitory Management Guidelines. Anyone that accumulates 10 penalty points
will be asked to move out of the dorms.
2. Apartment listings – information and services (Contact: 02-29393091 ext.63252)
（1）If you are not assigned to a dorm room you can go in person to the Student Housing Service Section to get information on apartment rentals near
the campus, or search for suitable housing on the website. Model Tenancy Agreement、Monthly Rental News Update and House Rental Manual
are also provided for free in the Student Housing Service Section.
（2）Webpage for apartment listings near campus can be found through the following path: → Homepage/Administration/Office of Student
Affairs/Student Housing Service/Off-campus Housing.
（3）You can ask the Student Housing Service Section for assistance in resolving problems with your apartment or conflicts with the landlord.
III Health Service Office(Health Center 2F):(Consultation Line for Freshmen Health Examination:02-82377431)
Health Examination for new students is required by the Ministry of Education and shall be completed by every newly-admitted student。
Please note that iNCCU account may not be accessible if the Health Examination is not completed within two weeks after the first day of
school.
IV Office of International Cooperation – Administration Building, 8th Floor
International students please contact the Office of International Cooperation (Contact: 02-29393091ext.67729)
Currently enrolled international students should take note of the following: According to the Immigration Law, international students
are required to apply for a visitor visa or resident visa before they enter Taiwan; international students must apply for ARC within 30
days after their arrival, renew ARC before the expired day. If there is change of address, students need to inform immigration agency
within 15 days.
2/2

text:
National Chengchi University Regulations for Direct
Admission to Ph.D. Programs
Revised and approved by the Academic Affairs Council Meeting in the 2nd
Semester of the 1994-95 academic year on Jun 7, 1995
Revised and approved by the Academic Affairs Council Meeting in the 2nd
Semester of the 2006-07 academic year on Mar 26, 2007
Revised and approved by the Academic Affairs Council Meeting in the 2nd
Semester of the 2020-21 academic year on Jun 7, 2021
Issued by Letter No. Cheng Jiao Zih 1100018231, June 30, 2021
Article 4 Amended and approved by the Academic Affairs Council Meeting in
the 2nd Semester of the 2022 academic year on Mar 20, 2022
Issued by Letter No. Cheng Jiao Zih 1120011856, May 2, 2023
I. The National Chengchi University Regulations for Direct Admission to Ph.D. Programs
(hereinafter referred to as the "Regulations") are established by National Chengchi
University (NCCU) in accordance with Paragraph 4, Article 23 of the University Act and the
Direct Pursuit of Ph.D. Degree Regulations.
II. NCCU students and students of other institutions within the University System of Taiwan
(UST) are eligible to apply for direct admission to Ph.D. programs with the following
qualifications:
(I) Undergraduate students in the current graduating class with excellent academic grades
and who show research potential.
(II) Master's students who have completed their first semester of study with excellent
academic grades and who show research potential.
Standards and criteria for the aforementioned excellent academic grades and research
potential shall be designated by the respective department, institute, college, or degree
program of NCCU.
III. Ph.D. direct admission applicants should submit their application within the period
designated by the respective department, institute, college, or degree program of NCCU.
Applicants should submit recommendations from two referees (at the level of assistant
professor or above) of the department, institute, college, or degree program in which they are
enrolled or a relevant department, institute, college, or degree program, and any other
relevant documents stipulated by the respective department, institute, college, or degree
program.
IV. The quota of students who may be admitted directly to NCCU Ph.D. programs shall not
exceed 40 percent of the admission quota of doctoral students for the corresponding
academic year designated by the Ministry of Education (MoE) for the respective department,
institute, college, or degree program; such quota may be shifted between Ph.D. programs
under the same college. MoE regulations that direct admission to Ph.D. programs in other
universities shall not exceed 5 percent of the admission quota shall also apply.

The designated quota for Ph.D. programs of each department, institute, college, or degree
program specified in the preceding paragraph shall not be filled entirely by students enrolled
through direct admission. However, this restriction does not apply in either of the following
circumstances:
(I) The designated quota for the Ph.D. program of the department, institute, college, or
degree program is one student.
(II) Talent cultivation program or project approved by the Ministry of Education.
The quotas in the two preceding paragraphs shall be included in the total enrollment quota
for the university approved by the Ministry of Education for the given year.
V. All departments, institutes, colleges, and degree programs of NCCU shall convene relevant
meetings to assess the procedures and, if necessary, organize selection examinations after
receiving applications.
Upon confirming the applicants' eligibility to apply for direct admission to Ph.D. programs,
all departments, institutes, colleges, and degree programs of NCCU shall submit relevant
procedural resolutions of meetings, the list of new students admitted, and relevant documents
for verification by the President. The aforementioned shall be delivered to the Office of
Academic Affairs before July 31 every year for processing of applicants' status so that they
are successfully enrolled in the Ph.D. program.
VI. Students approved for direct admission to Ph.D. programs shall become first-year students of
the program. Upon admission, students shall comply with regulations as stipulated by each
department, institute, college, or degree program.
As mentioned in Item 1, Paragraph 1, Article 2, undergraduate students in the current
graduating class shall earn their Bachelor's degree in the academic year they are granted
direct admission to a Ph.D. program. Should applicants fail to acquire their Bachelor's degree
on time, they shall no longer be eligible for direct admission to such Ph.D. program.
VII. Should students admitted directly to Ph.D. programs of NCCU apply for termination of study
during their study period, fail to pass the doctoral candidates qualifying examination, fail to
pass the graduate degree examination, or fail to comply with Article 8 of these Regulations,
and intend to enroll in a Master's program instead, they can do so upon submitting
application documents and seeking the consent of the relevant review committee of the
department, institute, college, or degree program in which they are coursing the Ph.D.
program and of the department, institute, college, or degree program which offers their
desired Master's program , as well as receiving approval by the President.
Upon transferring to a Master's program as stated in the paragraph above, the period during
which students coursed the Ph.D. program shall not be counted towards the study period of
the Master's program.
VIII. At the expiration of the maximum period of study, students admitted directly to Ph.D.
programs who have passed their doctoral candidates qualifying examination but failed to

pass their graduate degree examination shall be conferred a Master's degree if their
dissertation is deemed by the Ph.D. Degree Examination Committee as conforming to the
standards of a Master's degree dissertation.
IX. These Regulations shall be approved by the Academic Affairs Meeting before taking effect.
The same shall apply to all subsequent amendments.

National Chengchi University Principles for Assisting Students Who Have
Suffered from Unexpected Major Disaster
Passed on December 21, 2015, by the Academic Affairs Meeting in its
2nd Meeting of the 1st Semester of the 2015 Academic Year
Article 1 These Principles are established in accordance with Article 28 of the
University Act of Taiwan, the Ministry of Education's Principles for
Assisting Students Who Have Suffered from Unexpected Major Disaster
at the College Level or Above, and National Chengchi University
Academic Regulations.
Article 2 The major disasters that prevent students from normal studies referred to
in the Principles shall be determined by the competent authority of
education. Students affected by major disasters as well as those students’
academic rights shall be processed in accordance with the Principles.
Article 3 Students who have registered for an entry exam for NCCU may submit
relevant medical certification documents to apply for special exam
services or apply for refund; such students may also check-in and
register by submitting relevant certification documents through a proxy
or by mail.
Article 4 New students may submit through mail the relevant certification
documents within the period specified in National Chengchi University
Academic Regulations to retain their admission qualifications. Students
who have retained admission qualifications but failed to complete
registration before the expiry date may, as determined by individual
requirements, request approval from the NCCU president to extend the
retention period of admission qualifications.
Article 5 Students may submit relevant certification documents within the period
specified in National Chengchi University Academic Regulations and
apply for delayed registration in writing or through mail.
Article 6 Students' minimum course credits for each semester are not restricted by
the minimum course requirements specified in National Chengchi
University Academic Regulations. Students who fail to reach the
minimum number of credits shall pay credit fees based on the number of
course credits for the applicable period and shall not be required to pay
the full tuition or miscellaneous fees.
Course selection in schools other than NCCU shall not be restricted to
make-up or supplementary courses, courses not offered by NCCU, or by
the number of course credits.
The department of the student may file an application to provide
synchronized or unsynchronized remote education methods for NCCU
courses to assist students with their studies, provided that the quality of
study can be assured.
Article 7 Teachers may adjust the evaluation standards for grading subjects based

on the conditions of individual students and may provide make-up exams
or other remedial measures for the purpose of processing the scores of
students.
Article 8 Students may, through mail, suspend their studies within the period
specified in the National Chengchi University Academic Regulations; if
the period in the semester or the suspension period has expired, students
may submit relevant certification documents to file special applications.
Article 9 Students may apply for special approval from the NCCU president for
the following items depending on their physical or mental condition and
requirements of study:
1. Duration of study: Duration of study can be extended by at most 4
years, in accordance with National Chengchi University Academic
Regulations.
2. Removal of restrictions on undergraduate students for expulsion
resulting from failed academic scores.
3. Retention of international dual degrees or exchange student
qualifications.
4. Students who were not able to transfer to a different department in
accordance with procedure but require adjustments to their major
department.
5. Relaxation of student graduation qualifications, provided students
meet the minimum graduation credit requirements of the relevant
department.
Article 10 Any matters that are not addressed shall be governed by related
regulations of the Ministry of Education and the National Chengchi
University Academic Regulations.
Article 11 The Principles have been implemented after the approval of a University
Affairs Meeting; the same shall apply to all subsequent amendments
thereto.

NCCU Rules Governing Foreign Language Graduation Examinations
Approved in the 2nd Office of Academic Affairs Meeting in the first semester of 2006 on 2006/12/25
Amendments approved in the 143rd School Affair Meeting on 2007/4/28
Confirmed in the 144th School Affair Meeting on 2007/6/21
Amendments approved in the 152nd School Affair Meeting on 2009/1/16
Confirmed in the 144th School Affair Meeting on 2007/6/21
Abolished by the 197th University Affairs Meeting,on 2018/1/5
Article 1 National Chengchi University (referred to hereinafter as NCCU) has
formulated the "Rules Governing Foreign Language Graduation Examinations"
(referred to hereinafter as the Rules) for the purpose of ensuring the standard of
students' foreign language skills.
Article 2 The foreign languages to which the Rules apply are English, Arabic,
Russian, Japanese, Korean, Turkish, French, German, and Spanish.
International students and oversea Chinese students may choose Chinese as
their foreign language.
Article 3 The Rules apply to undergraduate students accepted by NCCU in or after
the academic year of 2005; the Rules do not apply to the foreign language
proficiency examinations for students with disabilities.
The foreign language graduation examinations for international students and
oversea Chinese students shall exclude the official languages in their
countries of nationality. This regulation applies to students accepted in or
after 2009.
Article 4The deans and directors of different departments and programs will open a
zero-credit hour "foreign language proficiency" course, for which the former
shall not be given additional hourly wages. Students must meet the English
proficiency in Article 5 or the foreign language proficiency in Article 6.2 of
these Rules and approved by the deans or directors before being allowed to
graduate. Students' grades are recorded as either "passed" or "failed."
Article 5 A student meeting one of the following standards of English proficiency is
deemed as meeting the foreign language graduation standard set by NCCU:
(1) Passed the high-intermediate GEPT examination.
(2) Scored 500 or higher on TOEFL.

(3) Scored 173 or higher on TOEFL-CBT (Computer-based TOEFL).
(4) Scored 61 or higher on TOEFL-IBT (Internet-based test).
(5) Scored 5.5 or higher on IELTS (The International English Language
Testing System).
(6) Acquired PET or higher from Cambridge Certificate.
(7) Scored 600 or higher on TOEIC.
Article 6 Reaching other foreign language evaluation standards (see Appendix) is
deemed as meeting the foreign language graduation standard set by NCCU.
The standards regarding foreign languages may be expanded or reduced in
the future in accordance with the reviews by the Department of Foreign
Languages and Literatures.
Article 7 Low-income students in each department/program may apply to the Office
of Student Affairs for a 50% subsidization for their examination fees. The
application is limited to twice per person and an amount of 2,000 per
subsidy.
Article 8 After the scores are entered and approvals from the departments/programs
are given, students who failed to meet the requirements in Article 5 or 6 may
take a zero-credit hour foreign language course held by NCCU according to
the type of language they were originally tested for. Those who successfully
complete the course are deemed as meeting the foreign language graduation
standard set by NCCU.
Students must pay for the aforementioned course before enrollment;
however, the fee is waivered for low-income students.
Article 9Each college, department, and program is allowed to raise their examination
standard.
Article 10 These Rules are put into effect after being approved in the Office of
Academic Affairs Meeting and submitted to and approved in the School
Affair Meeting.

NATIONAL CHENGCHI UNIVERSITY
Shunwen Auditorium Management Regulations
October 7, 2009 Approved by the 621st Administrative Meeting
May 4, 2011 Amended and approved by the 632nd Administrative Meeting for Article 4
May 7, 2014 Amended and approved by the 653rd Administrative Meeting for the full
text
Article 1 National Chengchi University (NCCU or "the University")
establishes these regulations to facilitate the management of the
Shunwen Auditorium (hereinafter referred to as the "Auditorium").
Article 2 The primary use of the Auditorium is for scheduled classes.
Remaining time slots may be allocated for use by internal university
units, prioritized as follows:
1) Large-class general education courses.
2) Large-class integrated courses.
3) Other large-class courses.
4) University-wide large-scale events.
Article 3 The use of the Auditorium must align with the operating hours of the
Arts and Culture Center. Exceptions may be made with special
project approval.
Article 4 Management responsibilities related to the Auditorium are assigned
as follows:
1) Usage Review Unit: Instruction Resource, Office of
Academic Affairs.
2) Access Control Unit:
a. During office hours: General Education Center.
b. Outside office hours: Arts and Culture Center, Office
of Student Affairs.
Article 5 The use of the Auditorium is limited to NCCU’s teaching, research,
and administrative units.
Units intending to use the Auditorium must submit an application
form to the Instruction Resource, Office of Academic Affairs, at least
two weeks in advance. Upon approval, the management fee must be
paid within one week.
If any of the following situations occur during use, the managing unit
has the right to terminate usage immediately. Fees already paid will
not be refunded, and applications from the unit will not be accepted
for one year. In severe cases, the matter will be reported to the
university for further action:
1) Subletting the venue to others without authorization.
2) Misuse of the venue inconsistent with the application details.
3) Violation of government laws or university regulations.

4) Engaging in any commercial activities.
Article 6 Except for official university courses and those specially approved,
all uses of the Auditorium are subject to the following fees:
1) Equipment Operation Fee: Units must provide their own
equipment operators. If unable to do so, they must hire
designated contractors or trained personnel from the General
Education Center, with costs borne by the user.
2) Cleaning and Management Fee: Charged by the hour, rounded
up to the nearest hour, at NT$500 per hour.
3) Overtime and Related Fees: Applicable for usage outside
office hours.
For official university courses, up to five sessions per subject are
exempt from fees. Additional sessions require special approval and
are subject to the fees outlined above.
Courses for in-service programs, extension education, or self-funded
programs must adhere to the first clause regarding fees.
Article 7 Units using the Auditorium must strictly comply with the prohibition
of food and beverages. After use, they are responsible for cleaning
the venue and restoring it to its original condition.
Users are responsible for restoring or compensating for any damage
to equipment or property caused during use.
Article 8 The Regulations shall be passed by the Administrative Meeting, and
then promulgated and implemented by the President. Any
amendments shall be processed accordingly.

title: law90b.pdf
text:
National Chengchi University Guidelines for Review of Violations of
Academic Ethics
Approved by the 673rd Administrative Meeting on December 6, 2017
Issued by Letter No. Cheng JiaoXiao Zih 1060038759, December 28, 2017
Article 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,10,11and Regulation Title Amended and Approved by the 688rd Administrative Meeting on March
3, 2020
Issued by Letter No. Cheng JiaoXiao Zih 1100008810, March 31, 2020
Article 1 This policy has been established by National Chengchi University (NCCU) to process
violations of academic ethics involving current or graduated students which occurred
during their study at NCCU in accordance with Degree Conferral Law, Enforcement
Rules of Degree Conferral Law, Ministry of Education Principles for Processing
Academic Ethics Incidents at the College Level and Above, NCCU University
Regulations, Guidelines for Graduate Degree Examinations, and Student Reward and
Punishment Policy.
Article 2 A violation of academic ethics refers to any of the following situations that presents in
the academic work of an NCCU student:
A. Fabrication: Creating non-existent information in an application, research data, or
research results.
B. Falsification: False altering of information in an application, research data, or
research results.
C. Plagiarism: Using, without proper citation, the information of others in an
application, research data, or research results. Improper citation, when deemed
serious, will be considered plagiarism.
D. Presenting work that has been written by someone other than the student him or
herself.
E. Releasing a duplicated publication without noting it as a duplication.
F. Substantial citations of one's own publications in a research project or thesis
without proper citation thereof.
G. Publishing a translation as an original publication without noting it as a
translation.
H. Other actions in violation of academic ethics.
Article 3 If a dissertation or works, achievement certificates, together with a written report,
technical report, or professional practice report replacing a dissertation in accordance
with Articles 7 and 9 of the Degree Conferral Act, is found via being reported or upon
being discovered by NCCU, within its authority, to have been involved in any of the
conducts described in the Subparagraphs of Article 2 herein, that student's conduct will
be investigated, deliberated, and handled in compliance with these Guidelines.
Article 4 The NCCU Office of Academic Affairs shall be the competent authority to process

relevant cases.
A report should be submitted under the real name and contact information of the
informant, along with an actual subject, contents, and evidence. The report will be
processed after the information is verified. NCCU maintains the absolute confidentiality
of informants.
If the identification information provided by the informant is false, the report will be
regarded as an anonymous report.
If a report is filed in the manner of the preceding Paragraph, where an anonymous
informant accuses a subject, provides details of the violation, and there is sufficient
evidence thereof, the report will be processed according to Paragraph 2.
All departments, institutions, or offices affiliated to NCCU shall prepare relevant
documents and report to the Office of Academic Affairs within their authority if they
detect the aforementioned matters related to academic ethics.
Article 5 The cases should be transferred to the department of the accused after received by the
Office of Academic Affairs.
Department should form an Investigation Committee within 10 days after received the
cases from the Office of Academic Affairs. The formation, meeting, and resolution of
the Committee must adhere to the following:
A. The Committee consists of 7 to 11 members, and is convened by the chair of the
department of the accused. The department head recommends the other
Committee members who are university and external professional scholars and
submit to the dean of the college for appointment. The list of the Committee
members must remain confidential.
B. The formation of the Investigation Committee must consist of at least one
non-NCCU member and must include a legal professional; the number of each of
the genders of the committee members shall not be less than one-third of the total
committee members.
C. If the convener must recuse himself or herself from the meeting, a member of the
Committee will be elected to chair the meeting.
D. Meetings must be held with the attendance of at least two-thirds of its members;
resolutions must have the agreement of at least two-thirds of the attending
members.
The Committee shall notify the accused to, within 2 weeks of notification, submit a
written defense or attend the meeting to present a statement in person in response to the
accusations. If the accused fails to do so by the allotted deadline, he or she will be
considered to have forfeited the right to submit a defense or present a statement.
Where deemed necessary by the Committee, the investigation panel may obtain
statements from the accused person's advising professor.
The Committee shall complete the investigation one month within its formation and
may extend the investigation for another one month if deemed necessary. The

Committee shall submit the investigation report, meeting minutes, specific conclusion
on whether the conduct is in violation of the academic ethics described in the
Subparagraphs of Article 2, and a disciplinary action suggestion to the college to which
the Committee is affiliated for review.
Article 6 The college of the accused should form a Review Committee and conduct an
examination after received the investigation report, meeting minutes, specific
conclusion and disciplinary action suggestion from the Investigation Committee of
department. The formation, meeting, and resolution of the Review Committee of college
must adhere to the following:
A. The Committee consists of 5 to 7 members, and is convened by the dean of the
college. The dean recommends other 4 to 6 members of Committee who are
university and external professional scholars and submit to the principal for
appointment. The list of the Committee members must remain confidential.
B. Over half of the Review Committee members must be non-NCCU members, and
the number of each of the genders of the committee members shall not be less
than one-third of the total committee members.
C. If the convener must recuse himself or herself from the meeting, a member of the
Committee will be elected to chair the meeting
D. Meetings must be held with the attendance of at least two-thirds of its members;
resolutions must have the agreement of at least two-thirds of the attending
members.
The Committee shall conduct a review of the investigation report, specific conclusion,
and disciplinary action suggestions. If necessary, the Committee shall notify the accused
or his/her advising professor to submit a written defense or attend the meeting to present
a statement in person in response to the accusations. If the accused fails to do so, he or
she will be considered to have forfeited the right to submit a defense or present a
statement.
If the Review Committee has doubts on the Investigation Committee's investigation
report and disciplinary action suggestions, the Review Committee shall conduct its own
investigation and make resolutions for the disciplinary actions.
The Review Committee shall complete the review within one month after receiving the
investigation report from the Investigation Committee and may extend the review for
another one month if deemed necessary.
Once the review results and disciplinary action suggestions are submitted to the Office
of Academic Affairs and NCCU President for approval, the Office of Academic Affairs
shall handle the subsequent administrative procedures accordingly.
Article 7 A Committee member and person who participates in relevant procedures must recuse
him or herself if the following relations or conditions with the accused are involved:
A. A relationship as a spouse or blood relative within the fourth degree of kinship; or
relative by marriage within the third degree of kinship.

B. An advisor-student relationship involving a doctoral or master's degree
dissertation (including works similar to a degree dissertation) and degree exam
committee member.
C. Researcher or co-author involved in collaboration within the last 3 years on the
presentation of a paper or research results.
D. An on-going joint research project during the investigation of said case.
E. A current or previous agent ad litem or assistant for the accused.
In any of the following circumstances, the accused may request that a Committee
member recuse him or herself:
A. Where the Committee member fails to recuse him or herself in spite of the
existence of any of the circumstances specified in the preceding Paragraph.
B. Where there are concrete facts to sufficiently support the belief that the member is
likely to be biased in the exercise of his or her duties.
Where a Committee member entails any of the circumstances specified in Paragraph 1
but fails to recuse himself or herself, or where the Committee member is likely to be
biased in the exercise of his or her duties, the Committee shall then invoke the authority
of position to demand that Committee member to recuse him or herself.
Article 8 If the accused involved in the reported case is found unequivocally in violation of
academic ethics, the disciplinary actions are as follows:
A. In accordance with the Degree Conferral Act, the degree of the accused shall be
revoked and the accused will be recorded as having been forced to withdraw from
NCCU if the accused is found involved in fraud, alteration, plagiarism, ghost
writing or other fraudulent behaviors.
B. The committee should consider circumstances which the academic ethics
violation is less severe than that in the preceding Subparagraph, the accused will
be ordered to rectify the violation, provide a public apology, or be subjected to
other proper disciplinary actions within a limited time period.
Article 9 After the review and resolution from the Review Committee, the Office of Academic
Affairs will handle the following matters to the reported case in accordance with
Paragraph 6, Article 6 of the Guidelines:
A. Notifying informant and accused of disciplinary action in writing.
B. If a student's degree is revoked as a result of a violation, the revocation of the
degree will be announced by NCCU, and the diploma bestowed on the accused
will be retrieved. Other universities will be informed of the revocation and
annulment, and letters will be sent to the National Central Library and NCCU
library to request the withdrawal of the hard copies and electronic files of the
accused's dissertation.
Article 10 The accused may submit an appeal to the Ministry of Education in accordance with
relevant procedures within thirty days following the day of receiving the review results
in written form if the accused is not satisfied with the results.

Article 11 After resolution, the reported case on violation of academic ethics will not be
investigated and reviewed again unless there have been new substantial facts or new
evidence. The Office of Academic Affairs may respond to the informant with the prior
resolution without further action.
Article 12 The advising professor of the accused whose degree dissertation is withdrawn by
NCCU shall be responsible for negligence in dissertation supervision, and further action
will be taken by the department or institution of the advising professor.
Article 13 Any matters that are not addressed in this policy will be governed by the relevant
regulations of the Ministry of Education and NCCU.
Article 14 These Guidelines have been announced and are implemented upon the approval of the
Administrative Committee meeting. The same procedure will apply to all subsequent
amendments thereto.

text:
National Chengchi University Principles for Student Course Selection and
Credit Recognition in Case of Required Courses Table Changes
Approved by Academic Affairs Meeting of the 2nd semester of academic year 2020 on June 8, 2020.
I. These principles were formulated in order to facilitate student course selection
and credit recognition w hen the University’s departments and institutes change
their table of required courses (hereafter known as the course table), or during
the transition period between old and new course tables.
II. Students should take courses based on their department or institute’s course
table for the academic year they entered the University, except when they
suspended their studies immediate upon entry or retained their student status, in
which case they should take courses based on the course table for the academic
year they resume their studies.
Students with a double major or minor should take courses based on the
department’s course table or course table for minor students for the academic
year their status as a double major or minor student was accepted.
Undergraduate students who transferred from another university or department,
and masters and doctoral students who transferred from another university,
should take courses based on the course table for the year of the department
they transferred into. Masters students who transferred from another institute
should take courses based on the course table of the department or institute for
the academic year that they first registered after the transfer.
III. When course offerings, number of credits, or number of semesters of a course
undergo changes in the course tables of departments or institutes or during the
transition period between new and old course tables, student course selection
and credit recognition should proceed based on the following principles.
(I) When required courses continue to be required, students should take
the courses as specified by the course table. Credits will be recognized
to the benefit of the student.
The number of recognized credits should not exceed 1/2 of the total
number of credits originally required for graduation for undergraduate
students. However, if the number of credits for required courses in the
original department has already exceeded 1/2 of the total number of
credits required for graduation, then the number of recognized credits
should not exceed the total number of credits originally required for
graduation. For graduate students, graduation credits should be
recognized based on the number of credits for courses taken by the
student.
(II) If a required course is no longer offered, or is changed to an elective
course or general studies course, students should in principle retake the
course or take an alternative course designated or accepted by the
department. Waivers for the required course should be granted only in
exceptional circumstances.
If the number of credits offered by a required course has changed
during the change to an elective course or general studies course,

credits should be recognized based on the principles outlined in the
previous subparagraph.
If the student takes an alternative course in lieu of a required course,
the number of credits recognized for the alternative course may not
exceed the maximum number of credits for the required course
specified in the original course table.
If the department or institute agrees to grant a waiver for the required
course, the student must still fulfill the minimum number of credits
required by the department or institute in order to graduate.
IV. This purpose of these Principles is to regulate situations in which departments
or institutes change the courses that they offer. If students wish to substitute
courses offered by another department or institute for courses offered by their
current department or institute, the maximum number of credits recognized by
the current department or institute will still apply.
V. These Principles shall take effect after the approval of the academic affairs
meeting. The same applies to all subsequent amendments.

[Promulgated on July 08, 2024]
National Chengchi University Undergraduate Student
Department Transfer Rules
March 09, 1977 Amended in the 420th Administrative Meeting
February 28, 1996 Amended in the 537th University Administration Meeting
October 09, 2002 Articles 1, 7, and 8 amended and approved in the 579th University Administration
Meeting
December 10, 2003 Article 1 amended and approved in the 587th University Administration Meeting
December 03, 2008 Article 7 amended and approved in the 617th University Administration Meeting
December 31, 2014 Articles 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, and 9 amended and approved in the 656th University
Administration Meeting
December 19,2016 Articles 3 approved by the 2nd Academic Affairs Meeting, fall semester, Academic Year
2016
December 28, 2016 Promulgated via official letter Cheng Chiao Tzu No. 105003828
February 17,2020 Articles 1, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 9 amended and approved by the Extraordinary Academic
Affairs Meeting, spring semester, Academic Year 2019
June 17, 2020 Referenced by Ministry of Education via official letter Tai Jiao Kao (II) Zih No.
1090075903
July 09, 2020 Promulgated via official letter Cheng Chiao Tzu No. 109001783
June 03,2024 Article 9 amended and Article 10 added were approved by the2nd Academic Affairs
Meeting, spring semester, Academic Year 2023
July 08, 2024 Promulgated via official letter Cheng Chiao Tzu No. 1130021899
Article 1 These rules have been established in accordance with the University Act and NCCU
University Regulations.
Article 2 All undergraduate students seeking to transfer departments within NCCU shall comply
with this rule.
Article 3 Each department may accept transfer students up to 20% of their newly allocated
admission quota but may not exceed the original quota set for first-year students for the
current academic year.
Transfer applications from the Mainland China Student Admissions Committee are
limited to the Mainland Chinese student enrollment quota of the destination department
(program) of the new academic year.
Article 4 Each department may set its own criteria for accepting transfer students; these criteria
shall be submitted to the Office of Academic Affairs and announced on a collective basis.
Each department may base the criteria on academic performance or excellence in other
areas or not set any qualifications and requirements at all.
Article 5 Undergraduate students who have completed the credits of one academic year or more
may apply for department transfer; the academic year the student is transferred into
shall be determined by the respective department.
Lower division transfer students must complete credits and mandatory subjects as
required by the academic year requirement (for the academic year the student wishes
to transfer into). The maximum limit of period of study shall be recalculated based
on the academic year of the destination department.
Every student may make one department transfer only. A transfer applicant may select
up to two departments on an application. The result will be decided by the department(s).
Program transfers within the same department shall proceed according to the transfer
policies.
Article 6 Allowances can be made at the verification of the school's counseling unit and the approval
of the chair of the current department and the chair of the destination department for the
following students who are unable to continue studies in the current department due to
misaligned interests or any other reasons:
1. International students.
2. Overseas Chinese students.

[Promulgated on July 08, 2024]
3. Hong Kong and Macao students.
4. Students with disability booklets or those issued by the Entrance Exam for Disabled
Students Committee.
Article 7 All department (program) transfer applications must be submitted within the specified
deadline. Those made by underage students cannot be submitted without the consent of
the student's parent/guardian. Applicants must obtain consent of the current department
before applying to the destination department. Once the destination department chair has
agreed to the transfer, the Office of Academic Affairs will approve the final list of
successful transfers based on the students' choices and submit it to the President for
approval and announcement.
Department transfers may not be modified or withdrawn once they have been
announced. Department transfer approval qualifications are cancelled for students who
have applied for suspension of studies during the semester of department transfer.
Article 8 Undergraduate students who have been admitted into NCCU via transfers or referral
programs prior to the 2010 academic year may not apply for department transfers
unless specially approved in an Academic Affairs Meeting.
Students admitted under the outlying-island admissions quota may not apply for
department transfers and shall be handled in accordance with "Regulations for
Recommendation for Admission of Outlying Island Students to Senior High Schools and
Above”.
Article 9 The transfer procedures following the establishment or adjustment of academic units are
as follows:
1. In cases where academic units are consolidated or recruitment is halted, if a new or
added academic unit with a closely related field of specialization is established,
applications for transferring all enrolled students to this new unit may be submitted
after reaching a consensus with the students through written communication or
meetings. With the agreement of the respective unit and the principal's approval,
students will continue their studies in the corresponding grade level.
2. If an academic unit establishes new groups within a program, in accordance with the
preceding provision, a special application may be submitted for the President's
approval to transfer all currently enrolled students who were not grouped into the
corresponding grade level of the new grouped program
3. Applications for transfer to new academic units or newly established groups should be
finalized one semester before the academic year in which the new unit or group is
officially sanctioned by the Ministry of Education.
Once the original academic unit has completed the procedure for transferring the
registration of enrolled students to another department (or group) as stated, students who
were pursuing double majors or minors at that unit will also have their records for these
programs adjusted accordingly.
The transfer process in the first item is not subject to the transfer quota specified in Article
3, Section 1, and this transfer does not count as one of the transfers allowed under Article
5, Section 3.
Article10 The Rules shall be passed by the Academic Affairs Meeting and then promulgated and
implemented. Any amendments shall be processed accordingly.

title: law113b.pdf
text:
National Chengchi University Undergraduate Student Guidance
Policy
January 10, 2020 Passed during the 270th University Council
Article 1 National Chengchi University (hereafter known as “the University”) has
formulated this Policy in order to support students in their learning, daily lives,
and physical and mental well-being; as well as to provide appropriate early
warning for problems and provide students with the necessary guidance.
Article 2 Student guidance should be initiated for students of the University in the
following circumstances:
I. If the student fails ½ or more of the total credits taken in the current semester.
II. If any of the following circumstances apply to a student at the end of their
third academic year:
(I) The student has not yet completed ½ of their department’s required
credits.
(II) The student has not yet received 88 graduation credits (including
credit exemption).
III. The student’s advisor has deemed that the student requires student guidance.
Article 3 If any of the circumstances described in Items 1 or 2 of the previous Article apply
to a student, the Office of Academic Affairs will notify the department, advisor,
student, and student’s parents. The student’s advisor will then initiate the
guidance process.
If all circumstances described in Item 2 of the previous Article apply to a student
at the end of their third academic year, the Office of Academic Affairs will notify
the Chair of the student’s department (hereafter known as the Chair) in addition
to the persons and offices described above; the Chair will then initiate the
guidance process.
Article 4 The process for student guidance in the University is as follows:
I. The student’s advisor conducts an interview with the student, and takes the
following actions based on the student’s circumstances:
(I) Confirms that the student requires student guidance.
(II) After the student gives consent, the advisor refers the student to
relevant guidance offices.
(III) The advisor reports the results of the interview to the Chair; the Chair
decides whether to convene a guidance meeting based on the student’s
circumstances.
II. The Chair conducts an interview with the student; the student’s advisor is a
required participant in the interview. The Chair takes the following actions
based on the student’s circumstances:

(I) Confirms that the student requires student guidance.
(II) After the student gives consent, the Chair refers the student to relevant
guidance offices.
(III) Convenes a guidance meeting.
III. The guidance meeting is chaired by the department Chair. The student’s
advisor is a required participant; the student’s parents, other instructors, the
Physical and Mental Health Center, the Career Development Center, the
Center of Teaching and Learning Development, or other guidance offices may
be invited to participate based on the student’s circumstances.
IV. Minutes of the guidance meeting should be taken by the department. All
guidance services provided by various officers should be recorded by relevant
office and personnel and preserved for future reference. The department
should track the progress of the student guidance.
For the student guidance process described above, the department should be
notified if the student is absent from scheduled interviews, meetings, or guidance
sessions three times or more in one month. The department may then contact the
student’s parents.
Article 5 The student’s advisor should record the student guidance process described in
Item 1 of the previous Article in the university affairs information system; the
department should receive a copy of all records.
A student’s current advisor, department Chair, and Dean may view the student’s
student guidance interview records.
Article 6 This policy is to be implemented and amended upon approval at the University
Council and promulgated by the Prisident of NCCU.
